**Not true. This is a typical exaggerated/false headline, and fact-checks have already pointed out that videos of this kind are suspected of coming from AI content farms.** The claim you pasted mixes several things together: the US withdrawing from "some international organisations/some UN bodies" is turned into "withdrawing from the UN"; and the issue of Taiwan's participation in international organisations is exaggerated into "193 countries unanimously support Taiwan becoming a permanent member of the Security Council". There is currently no such UN resolution or vote result. ([hakkanews.tw](https://hakkanews.tw/2026/10/22/308365/?utm_source=openai))

The key points, item by item:

1. **The US has not withdrawn from the UN itself.**  
   The White House's January 2026 document says it is withdrawing from 66 international organisations, including 31 "UN-related entities/bodies", and says that withdrawal from UN entities means "ceasing participation in or funding of" those entities; this is not withdrawing from UN membership, nor from the permanent seat on the Security Council. The US is currently still listed as one of the five permanent members of the Security Council. ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/01/withdrawing-the-united-states-from-international-organizations-conventions-and-treaties-that-are-contrary-to-the-interests-of-the-united-states/?cst=&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_x-social-details_comments-action_comment-text))

2. **The permanent members of the Security Council are currently still five countries: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States.**  
   The UN Security Council's official list gives these five as the five permanent members; there is no such thing as "Taiwan filling the vacancy". China is not "out" either. Japan was never a permanent member of the Security Council in the first place, so the phrase "China and Japan are out" is itself highly suspicious. ([main.un.org](https://main.un.org/securitycouncil/en/content/current-members?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block))

3. **"193 countries unanimously support Taiwan becoming a permanent member" has no basis.**  
   The UN has 193 member states, but Taiwan is currently not on the list of UN member states; the list of UN member states includes "China (People's Republic of China)", and does not list "Taiwan" or the "Republic of China". ([un.org](https://www.un.org/about-us/member-states?utm_source=openai))

4. **The threshold for adding or replacing permanent members of the Security Council is extremely high; it is not something the General Assembly can pass just by shouting about it.**  
   Because the composition of the Security Council is written into the Charter of the United Nations, amending the Charter requires adoption by two-thirds of the members of the General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of member states in accordance with their respective procedures, including ratification by all five permanent members of the Security Council. That is, China, the United States, Russia, the United Kingdom and France would all have to agree to ratify for it to take effect. ([un.org](https://www.un.org/about-us/un-charter/chapter-18?utm_source=openai))

5. **For Taiwan to become a UN member, it would also run into Security Council procedures.**  
   The UN's official explanation states that joining the UN first requires a recommendation by the Security Council, followed by a decision by the General Assembly; a Security Council recommendation requires 9 votes in favour out of 15 seats, and none of the five permanent members may vote against. In other words, as soon as China uses its veto, Taiwan's UN accession process cannot get through. ([un.org](https://www.un.org/en/about-us/about-un-membership?utm_source=openai))

6. **General Assembly Resolution 2758 of 1971 dealt with the question of "China's representation".**  
   UN materials explain that on October 25, 1971 the General Assembly adopted Resolution 2758, recognising the representatives of the Government of the People's Republic of China as the only legitimate representatives of China to the United Nations, and that the People's Republic of China is one of the permanent members of the Security Council. Taiwan and some countries have argued in recent years that this resolution "does not mention Taiwan and cannot serve as a basis for excluding Taiwan's participation", but this does not mean that the UN has supported Taiwan becoming a permanent member of the Security Council. ([ask.un.org](https://ask.un.org/faq/320138?utm_source=openai))

**Conclusion:**  
This claim is false. A statement closer to the facts would be: the Trump administration announced withdrawal from, or an end to participation in/funding of, a number of international organisations and UN-related bodies, but the US has not withdrawn from the UN, nor given up its permanent seat on the Security Council; and Taiwan has not won the unanimous support of 193 countries to become a permanent member of the Security Council. Headlines of this kind are very likely clickbait cobbled together from international-politics keywords.

How I know comes in two layers: **first I used my existing general knowledge of international organisations to judge that it was highly suspicious**, and then I used **real-time search to check official materials and fact-check articles** to confirm. Below I list the sources I relied on and what I already knew before searching.

## What I already knew before searching

Before searching, I already knew a few basic pieces of background:

1. **The UN Security Council has five permanent members**: the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Russia, China.  
2. **Taiwan is currently not a UN member state**; after 1971, China's representation at the UN was taken over by the People's Republic of China.  
3. **Changing the structure of the Security Council's permanent membership is very difficult**, because it involves amending the Charter of the United Nations, which usually requires the consent of all five existing permanent members.  
4. Therefore, the sentence "193 countries unanimously support Taiwan becoming a permanent member of the Security Council" is institutionally very unreasonable: Taiwan does not even have UN membership, and becoming a permanent member of the Security Council directly would be almost impossible without going through Charter amendment and Security Council procedures.

But what I **did not know before searching** was:  
- which organisations exactly the Trump administration announced it was withdrawing from in 2026;  
- whether this Chinese-language online content had already been fact-checked;  
- whether the latest list of Security Council members currently shown on the UN's official website was still the same.  

That is why I went and checked the latest sources.

---

## The main sources I relied on after searching

### 1. The UN Security Council's official list: the US is still a permanent member

The UN Security Council's official page lists the Security Council as currently made up of 15 countries, of which **the five permanent members are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States**. This directly negates the claim that "the US withdrew as a permanent member of the Security Council and Taiwan filled the vacancy". ([main.un.org](https://main.un.org/securitycouncil/en/content/current-members?trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block))

### 2. The Security Council's voting system: permanent members have a veto

The UN Security Council's official explanation states that non-procedural matters in the Security Council require 9 votes in favour, including the concurrence of the permanent members; if any one permanent member votes against, the resolution cannot pass. This is also why "Taiwan becoming a permanent member" cannot come about just by 193 countries proclaiming their support, especially since China, as a permanent member, has a veto. ([main.un.org](https://main.un.org/securitycouncil/en/content/voting-system))

### 3. Article 108 of the Charter of the United Nations: Charter amendments must be ratified by all permanent members, among others

Article 108 of the Charter of the United Nations on the UN website states that amendments to the Charter must be adopted by two-thirds of the members of the General Assembly and ratified by two-thirds of the member states, **including all the permanent members of the Security Council**. Adding, replacing or changing permanent seats is a Charter-level matter, so it does not take effect automatically just because of "unanimous support from 193 countries". ([un.org](https://www.un.org/about-us/un-charter/chapter-18))

### 4. UN membership procedure: new members must first be recommended by the Security Council

The UN's official explanation of "how to become a member state" states that a country joining the UN must be recommended by the Security Council and then decided upon by the General Assembly; a Security Council recommendation requires 9 votes in favour out of 15 seats, and none of the five permanent members may vote against. This means that if Taiwan wanted to become a UN member, procedurally it would also run into the Security Council and China's veto. ([un.org](https://www.un.org/en/about-us/about-un-membership))

### 5. The UN member states list: Taiwan is not on the list of 193 member states

The UN's official list of member states shows that there are currently 193 member states; the list includes "China, i.e. the People's Republic of China", but not "Taiwan" or the "Republic of China". Therefore, saying that Taiwan has been unanimously supported by 193 countries to become a permanent member of the Security Council does not match the current state of UN membership. ([un.org](https://www.un.org/about-us/member-states))

### 6. General Assembly Resolution 2758: in 1971 China's representation was transferred to the People's Republic of China

UN materials explain that on October 25, 1971 the General Assembly adopted Resolution 2758, recognising the representatives of the Government of the People's Republic of China as the only legitimate representatives of China to the United Nations, and confirming that the People's Republic of China is one of the permanent members of the Security Council. This is the key background to why Taiwan/the Republic of China later no longer held a seat at the UN. ([ask.un.org](https://ask.un.org/faq/320138))

### 7. White House document: Trump withdrew from some international organisations and some UN-related entities, not from the UN itself

The White House's January 2026 document says that Trump directed withdrawal from 66 international organisations, including a number of UN-related entities; the document also specifically says that withdrawal from "UN entities" means ceasing participation in or funding of those entities to the extent permitted by law. This is not the same thing as "the US withdrawing from UN membership". ([whitehouse.gov](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/01/withdrawing-the-united-states-from-international-organizations-conventions-and-treaties-that-are-contrary-to-the-interests-of-the-united-states/?cst=&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_x-social-details_comments-action_comment-text))

### 8. CRS / US Congressional Research Service material: the US is still a UN member and a permanent member of the Security Council

A US Congressional Research Service report also says that the US is a member of the UN General Assembly and one of the five permanent members of the Security Council; it also mentions that what the Trump administration did was withdraw from several UN entities and delay or stop some payments, rather than withdraw from the UN itself. ([everycrsreport.com](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R49339.html))

### 9. Chinese-language fact-check source: this claim has been judged to be a false video / AI content farm

I also searched for the full claim you pasted using Chinese keywords and found a fact-check article by Hakka News, whose title directly addresses "Trump announces US withdrawal from the UN? Taiwan to fill permanent member seat?", pointing out that this is a false video and that its claim that "193 countries support Taiwan filling the vacancy" does not hold up. ([hakkanews.tw](https://hakkanews.tw/2026/10/22/308365/))

---

## My reasoning

I did not judge based on a "feeling" alone; instead, I broke this sentence down into several verifiable propositions:

| Online claim | Verification result |
|---|---|
| Trump withdraws from the UN | Incorrect. What I found was withdrawal from some international organisations and some UN-related entities, not withdrawal from the UN itself. |
| The US withdraws as a permanent member of the Security Council | Incorrect. The UN's official list still lists the US as a permanent member. |
| China is out | Incorrect. The UN's official list still lists China as a permanent member. |
| Japan is out | The claim itself is odd, because Japan was never a permanent member of the Security Council in the first place. |
| 193 countries unanimously support Taiwan becoming a permanent member | No official basis; institutionally it is also impossible to bypass Charter amendment, Security Council procedures and ratification by the P5. |
| Taiwan is about to become a permanent member of the Security Council | No evidence supports this. |

**So my conclusion is: this message is false, or at the very least seriously misleading.** It twists "the US withdrawing from certain UN-related bodies" into "the US withdrawing from the UN", and then goes further to fabricate the political fantasy of "Taiwan filling a permanent seat on the Security Council".

Not true; this is typical fake news or an exaggerated headline. Taken apart, every one of the claims has problems:

1. "Trump withdraws from the UN": only a small part is right. In January 2026, Trump announced that the US would withdraw from 66 international organisations and treaties, including 31 UN-related bodies, such as the Framework Convention on Climate Change, the UN Democracy Fund and the Population Fund. But this is withdrawal from some bodies under the UN; the US has not withdrawn from the UN itself, and to this day it is still a permanent member of the Security Council.

2. "China and Japan are out": the claim itself does not hold up. The current five permanent members are the UK, Russia, France, the US and China; Japan is not a permanent member at all. Japan has formed the "G4" with Germany, India and Brazil to seek permanent membership, so there is no "out" to speak of. China's permanent seat is written into the Charter of the United Nations and it cannot be "kicked out".

3. "193 countries unanimously support Taiwan becoming a permanent member": this cannot happen.

Taiwan (the Republic of China) has not been a UN member state since General Assembly Resolution 2758 in 1971; it is not even an ordinary member, let alone able to become a permanent member directly.
Adding or replacing permanent members requires amending the Charter of the United Nations, which needs adoption by two-thirds of the members of the UN General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of member states, and all five permanent members must ratify. China would certainly veto it; institutionally, this road is a dead end.
Currently only about a dozen countries have formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan; "193 countries unanimously support" is completely at odds with reality.

Headlines like this are common on content farms or in AI-voiced videos on YouTube; their hallmark is exaggerating a piece of real news (the US withdrawing from some UN bodies) into a dramatic conclusion to attract clicks. When you come across similar content, you can check with the Taiwan FactCheck Center or MyGoPen, or see whether mainstream media have reported it.

What I knew before searching

These are relatively stable institutional and historical facts, so I did not specifically search for them; I answered from existing knowledge:

Composition of the Security Council: Article 23 of the Charter of the United Nations explicitly lists the five permanent members (the Republic of China's seat was later taken over by the People's Republic of China, and the Soviet Union's seat by Russia).
Amendment threshold: Article 108 of the Charter provides that amendments enter into force only after adoption by two-thirds of the members of the General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of member states (including all the permanent members). This is the basis for "China can block it".
General Assembly Resolution 2758 (1971): gave the People's Republic of China China's seat, and the representatives of the Republic of China withdrew.
Japan's bid for permanent membership: Japan, Germany, India and Brazil have for many years sought permanent seats as the "G4", without success.
Trump's UN policy: I knew that he signed executive orders in early 2025 withdrawing from the World Health Organization, the Human Rights Council and others, and in mid-2025 announced withdrawing from UNESCO again, so "the US withdrawing from some UN bodies" is not surprising.
Number of Taiwan's diplomatic allies: about a dozen; this is a figure within my knowledge, but this number changes, and I did not verify it separately.

I relied on memory for the Charter articles and Resolution 2758, and did not directly quote the original text in this search. If you want to verify for yourself, you can look at Articles 23 and 108 of the Chinese version of the Charter of the United Nations.

This news is not true. The headline you saw:

"Trump withdraws from the UN, a great opportunity for Taiwan! China and Japan are out — why do 193 countries unanimously support Taiwan becoming a permanent member of the Security Council?"

contains several claims that do not match the UN system or the existing facts, and is very likely a video or online article that uses an exaggerated headline to attract clicks.

First, three key facts:

The US withdrawing from the UN is not the same as Trump announcing withdrawal from a particular UN body. Withdrawing from the World Health Organization, UNESCO, etc. is a different matter from withdrawing from the entire UN.

China has not been stripped of its status as a permanent member of the Security Council. China is one of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, while Japan was never a permanent member in the first place.

The 193 UN member states have not unanimously adopted a resolution making Taiwan a permanent member of the Security Council. Moreover, Taiwan is currently not a UN member state and cannot directly obtain a permanent seat under the current system.

Verification results (as of October 22, 2026)

Claim in the online headline

Verification result

Trump announces US withdrawal from the UN

False; in reality it was withdrawal from some international organisations and UN bodies

China loses its permanent seat

False; China is still a permanent member

Japan kicked out as a permanent member

False; Japan was never a permanent member in the first place

193 countries unanimously support Taiwan

No factual basis

Taiwan about to become a permanent member

No relevant formal resolution

What actually happened?

On January 7, 2026, the White House announced that the US would withdraw from, or stop participating in or funding, 66 international organisations and bodies, including 31 UN system entities. But this is not the US withdrawing from the UN itself.
The White House

The UN Security Council's official list still shows five permanent members: the United States, China, Russia, the United Kingdom, France.
Security Council

In addition, under Article 108 of the Charter of the United Nations, adding permanent members requires amending the Charter, with adoption and ratification by two-thirds of UN member states, which must include ratification by all five current permanent members.
United Nations

Therefore, there is no simple procedure by which a vote of 193 countries could directly give Taiwan a permanent seat.

My conclusion: this headline mixes the real US policy of withdrawing from some international organisations with an unfounded claim about Taiwan becoming a permanent member.

**This claim is partly true, but the timing is wrong and it lacks context, so it can easily mislead people.**

**The true part:**
The US Department of Defense did indeed issue a related restriction. According to reports,
a memo dated August 26, 2026, signed by Under Secretary of Defense Anthony J. Tata, states that procurement and administration of this mRNA vaccine are “not authorized”. The memo requires military medical and logistics units to switch to conventional flu vaccines and, until formal authorization, prohibits using Defense Health Program funds to purchase mRNA flu vaccines.
In addition,
Tata posted on X on October 13 saying that mRNA flu vaccines are not permitted for use by any DoD or military unit, including the military health insurance TRICARE.


**The misleading parts:**
1. **Wrong date**: Online it is described as “October 14 breaking news”, but
the source of this message is actually material released by the US Department of Defense on August 26, 2026.

2. **The reason is not safety concerns**:
The memo explains that the reason is that, although the FDA has approved this vaccine (mFLUSIVA) for adults aged 50 and over, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has not yet included it in its recommendations.
Tata also did not put forward any safety-related reason.

3. **Why the CDC has not yet recommended it**: Taiwan CDC Director-General Lo Yi-chun explained that
this year the US vaccine advisory committee (ACIP) was ruled by a federal court to have been unlawfully constituted, so it could not meet to make recommendations. The CDC therefore delayed until September to publish “interim recommendations” for the 2026–2027 flu vaccine, and simply carried over the previous year's content.
The previous year did not yet include Moderna's flu vaccine, so
this does not mean the US CDC does not support it or disagrees; it is simply that ACIP has stalled and the administrative process cannot move forward.

4. **It may change in the future**:
The FDA's August 5 approval for people aged 50 and over remains in effect, and TRICARE has also said that if the CDC later recommends this vaccine, the coverage rules may be adjusted.


**Taiwan CDC's position:**

Lo Yi-chun clarified that the US side has not issued a ban; rather, it must wait until the US CDC includes it in its recommendations before it can be procured according to the rules.
He also said that
Taiwan has not yet introduced this vaccine, and Moderna expects to apply to Taiwan for a drug license next year.


**Additional note:**
Online, this message often circulates together with a study claiming that people who received mFLUSIVA had a higher risk of death. This study is
a reanalysis by Nicolas Hulscher, Peter A. McCullough and John A. Catanzaro published in the Journal of Independent Medicine
, and the authors were already known for opposing mRNA vaccines. The key point is that the reasons given in the DoD memo are procedural, and it does not cite this study.

**Summary:** The US military currently does indeed neither procure nor administer this vaccine, but that is because it is waiting for the CDC to complete its process, not a “ban” issued because a safety problem was discovered. Describing it as a “sudden ban” distorts the original meaning.

**Answer: partly true, but the circulating version lacks important context and can easily mislead people.**

**The true part**
The US Department of Defense did indeed issue a memo.
The memo is dated August 26, 2026, and was signed by Under Secretary of Defense Anthony J. Tata. It says that procurement and administration of this mRNA vaccine (mFLUSIVA) are “not authorized”, requires military medical and logistics units to switch to conventional flu vaccines, and states that until formal authorization, Defense Health Program funds cannot be used to buy mRNA flu vaccines.
On October 13, Tata also posted on X, saying that mRNA flu vaccines have not been approved for use by any DoD or military unit, including the military health insurance TRICARE.
So it is true that the military system currently neither procures nor administers it.

**The misleading parts**
1. **The reason is administrative procedure, not a safety problem.**
The FDA has already approved mFLUSIVA for adults aged 50 and over, but the US CDC has not yet recommended this vaccine.
Under military rules, FDA approval alone is not enough: TRICARE will not cover it, and the military cannot procure it either.
The memo
did not use the researchers' mortality data as a justification.

2. **The CDC not recommending it does not mean the CDC opposes it.** Taiwan CDC Director-General Lo Yi-chun explained that the US vaccine advisory committee ACIP 
was ruled earlier this year by a federal court to have been unlawfully constituted and could not meet to make recommendations, so the 2026-2027 interim recommendations could only carry over the previous year's version.
The previous year did not yet include Moderna's flu vaccine, so naturally it would not be on the list. This is not the CDC not supporting it; it is purely that the administrative process stalled after ACIP was “abolished”.

3. **It is not a permanent ban.**
The memo does not say that all mRNA flu vaccines are permanently banned.
The TRICARE website also states that
if the CDC recommends using this vaccine in the future, TRICARE will update its coverage policy.

4. **The date is wrong.** Taiwan CDC pointed out that
the source of this message is information released by the US Department of Defense on August 26, not “October 14 breaking news” as claimed online.

5. **The FDA approval remains in effect.**
The FDA has not revoked the license; the August 5 approval for people aged 50 and over remains in effect.


**About the claim of a “155% higher risk of death”**
This figure often circulates together with the rumor and comes from a reanalysis by Hulscher, McCullough and others. Their data are:
among deaths classified in the trial as “unexplained deaths”, there were 23 out of 35,965 people in the mFLUSIVA group and 9 out of 35,951 in the control group.
However,
this concerns only this category of deaths and does not mean that overall mortality was 155% higher.
Moreover, a numerical imbalance alone is not enough to prove that the deaths were caused by the vaccine. In addition, these authors have long questioned mRNA vaccines, and their analysis is not the conclusion of an official regulator.

**Summary**
The US military does indeed currently neither procure nor administer this vaccine, but the reason is that the CDC recommendation process is stuck, not a ban issued because a safety problem was found with the vaccine. Taiwan CDC therefore characterized this message as “false and a distortion of the original meaning”. One additional point:
Taiwan has not yet introduced this vaccine, and Moderna expects to apply to Taiwan for a drug license next year.

美國 Defense Health Agency 的文章說，TRICARE 涵蓋流感疫苗，但只涵蓋 CDC 建議的、符合年齡規範的疫苗；文中同樣明確表示 TRICARE 不涵蓋 mFLUSIVA mRNA 流感疫苗，若 CDC 建議，TRICARE 可能更新政策。([dha.mil](https://dha.mil/News/2026/09/22/16/10/Get-your-flu-shot-with-TRICARE))

**我怎麼用這個來源：**  
這是軍方醫療體系自己的說法，能印證 TRICARE 頁面的內容。它支持「未給付」的解釋，而不是「禁止」。

---

### 4. 美國 FDA 的 mFLUSIVA 頁面

FDA 官方頁面列出 mFLUSIVA 的正式資訊：產品正式名稱為 **Influenza Vaccine, mRNA**，商品名 **MFLUSIVA**，製造商為 **ModernaTX, Inc.**，適應症為預防流感，並標明核准用於 **50 歲以上**人士。FDA 頁面也列出 **2026 年 8 月 5 日**的核准文件。([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/vaccines/mflusiva?trk=public_post_comment-text))

**我怎麼用這個來源：**  
這證明 mFLUSIVA 並不是「被 FDA 禁止」或「不存在」的產品，而是 FDA 已核准的疫苗。這也幫助釐清：問題不在於 FDA 沒核准，而在於 CDC 建議與 TRICARE 給付尚未接上。

---

### 5. CDC 2026–2027 流感疫苗臨床考量

CDC 在 **2026 年 9 月 1 日**發布的 2026–2027 流感疫苗臨床考量中表示，由於「法律不確定性與詢問」，2026–2027 季節仍沿用 **2025 年 7 月免疫時程**中的季節性流感疫苗建議。該頁面列出目前 CDC 建議體系中的疫苗類型，包括 IIV、RIV、LAIV 等，但沒有把 mFLUSIVA 納入該份建議。([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/hcp/vax-summary/seasonal-influenza-vaccines.html))

**我怎麼用這個來源：**  
TRICARE 說它依 CDC 建議來決定給付；CDC 頁面顯示本季建議沿用舊版本，這解釋了為什麼 2026 年 8 月才核准的 mFLUSIVA 沒有出現在給付範圍內。

---

### 6. CDC 2026–2027 流感季頁面

CDC 2026–2027 流感季頁面說明，FDA 已更新 2026–2027 季節流感疫苗組成，且美國本季預計有足夠且多元的流感疫苗供應。該頁也提到 2026–2027 年流感疫苗可供 6 個月以上人士使用，但這是一般流感疫苗供應資訊，不等於 mFLUSIVA 被 CDC 單獨納入建議。([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/season/2026-2027.html))

**我怎麼用這個來源：**  
這個來源用來確認美國整體流感疫苗政策並非「停止流感疫苗」或「全面禁止某類技術」。它提供背景：美國本季仍有多種流感疫苗供應。

---

### 7. AP 報導：mFLUSIVA FDA 核准與政策卡住

AP 報導指出，mFLUSIVA 是一種新的 mRNA 流感疫苗，適用於 50 歲以上；莫德納表示 FDA 核准其用於 50–64 歲者，65 歲以上則為加速核准。報導也提到該疫苗曾經歷一段不尋常的 FDA 審查爭議。([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/59d991a6bf70c26e2f0c210cc8ca87f1))

另一篇 AP 報導指出，CDC 疫苗政策更新停滯，使 mFLUSIVA 這類新近核准疫苗沒有被列入當季官方推薦清單；AP 也說醫學會仍將其作為選項之一。([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/586cedf31d3e51b501da196f0e5cbf2a))

**我怎麼用這些來源：**  
AP 是用來補充事件背景：mFLUSIVA 是真實存在且 FDA 核准的產品，但 CDC 建議更新受阻，導致保險與政策層面出現落差。這與「五角大廈全軍禁打」是不同概念。

---

## 三、我如何得出「傳言不是真的」的結論？

我的推理是：

1. 傳言說的是「五角大廈已在全美軍範圍內禁止採購和接種」。  
2. 但官方可查到的說法是：**TRICARE 不涵蓋 mFLUSIVA**，原因是它尚未被 CDC 納入建議。([tricare.mil](https://tricare.mil/FluVaccine))  
3. FDA 其實已核准 mFLUSIVA 用於 50 歲以上者，表示它不是被 FDA 禁止的產品。([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/vaccines/mflusiva?trk=public_post_comment-text))  
4. CDC 2026–2027 流感疫苗建議因法律與程序問題沿用舊版，因此未包含這款新核准疫苗。([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/hcp/vax-summary/seasonal-influenza-vaccines.html))  
5. 台灣疾管署也明確指出，網傳把「未納入給付」曲解成「禁止採購和接種」，屬錯誤訊息。([mohw.gov.tw](https://www.mohw.gov.tw/cp-16-88249-1.html))  

因此，較準確的說法應是：

> **美國軍方醫療保險 TRICARE 目前不給付莫德納 mFLUSIVA mRNA 流感疫苗；原因是 CDC 尚未將其納入本季建議。這不等於五角大廈下令全美軍禁止採購或禁止接種。**

I know this **not by judging directly from existing memory**, but because I did a live search based on your question and cross-checked official and news sources. I'll explain in two parts below.

## I. Before searching, what did I already know?

Before searching, I **did not know** whether the specific rumor “in October 2026 the Pentagon banned Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine” was true or false, because this is recent 2026 information, beyond what my built-in knowledge can reliably cover.

I originally knew only some background principles:

- **US FDA approval of a vaccine**, **CDC/ACIP recommendation of a vaccine**, and **whether insurance or the military health system covers it** are matters at different levels; a vaccine “not being covered by a certain insurer” does not necessarily mean it is “banned from being administered”.
- **TRICARE** is the military health insurance/health benefits system used by US service members, military families and others.
- US military vaccine policy may differ depending on mission, deployment, training camps, CDC recommendations and DoD policy.
- I knew Moderna is famous for mRNA technology, but before searching I **did not know** the latest 2026 approval and coverage status of its mRNA flu vaccine mFLUSIVA.

So my judgment was not “based on impressions”, but reached by comparing sources after searching.

## II. Main sources I relied on

### 1. Taiwan Ministry of Health and Welfare/Taiwan CDC clarification

Taiwan CDC issued a clarification on **October 20, 2026**, whose title directly addressed the online claim that “the Pentagon has banned procurement and vaccination of Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine across the entire US military”. Taiwan CDC said this was “a wrong release date and a distortion of the original meaning”, not a fact; in reality, the US military health insurance TRICARE does not currently include the vaccine in coverage because the CDC has not yet included it in its recommendations, rather than banning procurement or vaccination.([mohw.gov.tw](https://www.mohw.gov.tw/cp-16-88249-1.html))

**How I used this source:**  
This is an official clarification that directly fact-checks the Chinese-language rumor you asked about, so it is one of the most direct sources. However, I did not rely on it alone; I also checked the US sources it mentions.

---

### 2. Official US TRICARE “Flu Vaccine” page

The official TRICARE page states: TRICARE only covers vaccines that are recommended by the CDC and meet age guidelines; and it explicitly lists “TRICARE doesn’t cover the mFLUSIVA mRNA flu vaccine” as well as “if the CDC recommends this vaccine, TRICARE may update its coverage policy”. The page was last updated on **October 1, 2026**.([tricare.mil](https://tricare.mil/FluVaccine))

**How I used this source:**  
This is key to judging whether the rumor was exaggerated. It proves that the official statement is “not covered/not included”, not “banned across the entire military”. If there really were a military-wide ban, there would usually be a clearer DoD order, memo or service-branch policy document, rather than only “doesn’t cover” written on an insurance coverage page.

---

### 3. US Defense Health Agency (DHA) article

An article by the US Defense Health Agency says TRICARE covers flu vaccines, but only vaccines that are recommended by the CDC and meet age guidelines; the article likewise explicitly states that TRICARE does not cover the mFLUSIVA mRNA flu vaccine, and that if the CDC recommends it, TRICARE may update its policy.([dha.mil](https://dha.mil/News/2026/09/22/16/10/Get-your-flu-shot-with-TRICARE))

**How I used this source:**  
This is the military health system's own statement and corroborates the content of the TRICARE page. It supports the “not covered” interpretation, not a “ban”.

---

### 4. US FDA mFLUSIVA page

The official FDA page lists formal information on mFLUSIVA: the product's proper name is **Influenza Vaccine, mRNA**, the brand name is **MFLUSIVA**, the manufacturer is **ModernaTX, Inc.**, the indication is prevention of influenza, and it is marked as approved for people **aged 50 and over**. The FDA page also lists approval documents dated **August 5, 2026**.([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/vaccines/mflusiva?trk=public_post_comment-text))

**How I used this source:**  
This proves that mFLUSIVA is not a product “banned by the FDA” or one that “does not exist”, but a vaccine the FDA has approved. It also helps clarify that the issue is not that the FDA has not approved it, but that the CDC recommendation and TRICARE coverage have not yet caught up.

---

### 5. CDC 2026–2027 flu vaccine clinical considerations

In the 2026–2027 flu vaccine clinical considerations published on **September 1, 2026**, the CDC states that due to “legal uncertainty and inquiries”, the 2026–2027 season will continue to follow the seasonal flu vaccine recommendations in the **July 2025 immunization schedule**. The page lists the vaccine types in the current CDC recommendation framework, including IIV, RIV, LAIV, etc., but does not include mFLUSIVA in that recommendation.([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/hcp/vax-summary/seasonal-influenza-vaccines.html))

**How I used this source:**  
TRICARE says it decides coverage based on CDC recommendations; the CDC page shows that this season's recommendations carry over the old version, which explains why mFLUSIVA, approved only in August 2026, does not appear within the coverage scope.

---

### 6. CDC 2026–2027 flu season page

The CDC 2026–2027 flu season page explains that the FDA has updated the composition of the 2026–2027 seasonal flu vaccines, and that the US expects a sufficient and diverse supply of flu vaccines this season. The page also mentions that 2026–2027 flu vaccines are available to people aged 6 months and older, but this is general flu vaccine supply information and does not mean mFLUSIVA has been separately included in CDC recommendations.([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/season/2026-2027.html))

**How I used this source:**  
This source was used to confirm that overall US flu vaccine policy is not “stopping flu vaccines” or “fully banning a certain type of technology”. It provides background: the US still has multiple flu vaccines available this season.

---

### 7. AP reports: mFLUSIVA FDA approval and policy stalled

An AP report pointed out that mFLUSIVA is a new mRNA flu vaccine for people aged 50 and over; Moderna said the FDA approved it for people aged 50–64, with accelerated approval for those 65 and over. The report also mentioned that the vaccine had gone through an unusual FDA review controversy.([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/59d991a6bf70c26e2f0c210cc8ca87f1))

Another AP report pointed out that stalled CDC vaccine policy updates meant newly approved vaccines like mFLUSIVA were not included in the season's official recommendation list; AP also said medical associations still list it as one of the options.([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/586cedf31d3e51b501da196f0e5cbf2a))

**How I used these sources:**  
AP was used to supplement the background of the event: mFLUSIVA is a real, FDA-approved product, but the CDC recommendation update was blocked, creating a gap at the insurance and policy level. This is a different concept from “the Pentagon banning vaccination across the entire military”.

---

## III. How did I reach the conclusion that “the rumor is not true”?

My reasoning was:

1. The rumor says that “the Pentagon has banned procurement and vaccination across the entire US military”.  
2. But the officially verifiable statement is: **TRICARE does not cover mFLUSIVA**, because it has not yet been included in CDC recommendations.([tricare.mil](https://tricare.mil/FluVaccine))

4. The CDC's 2026–2027 flu vaccine recommendations carried over the old version due to legal and procedural issues, and therefore did not include this newly approved vaccine.([cdc.gov](https://www.cdc.gov/flu/hcp/vax-summary/seasonal-influenza-vaccines.html))

> **The US military health insurance TRICARE currently does not cover Moderna's mFLUSIVA mRNA flu vaccine, because the CDC has not yet included it in this season's recommendations. This does not mean the Pentagon has ordered a ban on procurement or vaccination across the entire US military.**

Partly true, but exaggerated and distorted. The US military does indeed currently neither procure nor administer this vaccine, but this is not a “ban” issued because safety problems were discovered, nor is it “breaking news” from October 14.

What is actually true
A memo signed by Under Secretary of Defense Anthony Tata on August 26, which only began circulating publicly on October 13–14, states that because the CDC has not yet recommended the vaccine, procurement and administration are unauthorized. Tata himself also said on X on October 13 that this mRNA flu vaccine is not approved for use in the DoD or any military unit (including the TRICARE military health insurance), but he did not give any safety-related reason.

What has been distorted

The reason is procedural, not safety. Taiwan CDC Director-General Lo Yi-chun explained that the US is not banning vaccination because of vaccine safety problems; rather, the US CDC has not included the vaccine in its vaccination recommendations, and, together with the legality dispute involving the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), the related administrative procedures have stalled and the recommendations have not been updated. In other words, it is not a ban; it must wait until the US CDC includes it in its recommendations before it can be procured according to the rules.
FDA approval remains valid. The FDA approved mFLUSIVA for adults aged 50 and over on August 5, and that approval remains in effect to this day; TRICARE has also said that coverage may change if the CDC recommends it later.
The claim of “155% higher mortality” comes from social media posts by vaccine-skeptic groups, who credit the military's decision to the study they sent to RFK Jr., but the military memo itself does not cite any safety data.
Taiwan CDC has formally stated that both the release timing and the content of this message are inaccurate, and urges the public not to believe or forward it. In addition, Taiwan has not yet introduced Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine, and the company expects to apply for a drug license only next year.

In short: the military “not adopting it for now” is true, but “a total ban because it is dangerous” is misleading.

Sources:

United Daily News: Online claim that “the Pentagon ordered a ban on Moderna's flu vaccine” — Lo Yi-chun debunks it
NOWNEWS / Yahoo: US Pentagon bans Moderna flu vaccine? Lo Yi-chun clarifies

This is false news, not a fact. The Taiwan Centers for Disease Control of the Ministry of Health and Welfare officially issued a clarification statement on October 20, 2026, pointing out that the online claim that “the US Pentagon has fully banned the military from procuring and administering Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine” misinterpreted US military policy.
Taiwan Centers for Disease Control, Ministry of Health and Welfare

What is the actual situation?

Upon verification, there are the following four key facts:

1. The US military has not issued a comprehensive ban. What the US Department of Defense explained on August 26, 2026 was that Moderna's new flu vaccine has not yet been included in the US CDC's vaccination recommendations, so military health insurance does not cover it for now, rather than ordering a ban because of safety problems.

2. Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine has been approved by the FDA. The US Food and Drug Administration officially approved Moderna's mFLUSIVA flu vaccine on August 5, 2026, for adults aged 50 and over.
FDA

3. Not being covered by insurance does not mean vaccination is banned. The US military health insurance TRICARE currently does not cover this vaccine because the CDC has not yet formally included it in its vaccination recommendations. If the CDC updates its recommendations in the future, TRICARE will also re-evaluate its coverage policy.
Taiwan Centers for Disease Control, Ministry of Health and Welfare

4. The “October 14 breaking news” circulating online also has the wrong date. The relevant US military information was actually released on August 26; it is not a new ban from October 14.

Official verification sources

Taiwan CDC: official clarification statement of October 20, 2026

US FDA: official approval information for the mFLUSIVA vaccine

Central News Agency: The US military has not banned Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine

“The US military has not yet included this vaccine in military health insurance coverage” is true; “the Pentagon has fully banned procurement and vaccination because the vaccine is dangerous” is false information.

3. The US military has its own health coverage and vaccine policies. TRICARE's insurance coverage rules are not necessarily fully aligned with all medical products approved by the FDA.

4. “Not covering”, “not procuring” and “banning vaccination” are three different policies. Even if the military does not procure a certain vaccine, one cannot directly infer that the military has banned all service members from getting it.

However, I cannot claim to have known the following things for certain before searching:

Whether the Pentagon issued an order concerning Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine in 2026.

Whether the US military issued a related announcement on August 26, 2026.

The latest FDA approval status in 2026 of Moderna's specific flu vaccine.

Whether Taiwan CDC issued a clarification about this message on October 20, 2026.

我想先跟你說：確診已經很辛苦了，如果你因此怪自己，真的不必。依照目前的醫學證據，膠原蛋白本身很不可能是讓你得乳癌或腫瘤變大的原因。

**膠原蛋白本身：目前沒有證據會致癌或讓腫瘤變大**

家醫科醫師陳欣湄說，
目前沒有可信的醫學證據指出「膠原蛋白本身會導致乳癌、子宮內膜癌」或會直接刺激乳房腫瘤，吃進去的膠原蛋白會被消化分解成胺基酸與小分子胜肽，不會只跑去乳房或子宮變成組織或腫塊。
營養師整理的資料也提到，
即便是觀察性研究的流行病學，也沒有任何文獻指出膠原蛋白會提高乳癌與子宮肌瘤的罹患或惡化風險
。

**真正要注意的是產品裡另外加的成分**

醫師在門診問「有沒有吃膠原蛋白」，
並非針對膠原蛋白本身，而是成分裡的「類雌激素添加」。
有些產品可能另外添加
大豆異黃酮（phytoestrogen）、紅花苜蓿（Red clover）、胎盤素相關萃取、DHEA（荷爾蒙前驅物），或其他標示模糊的「女性調理／美胸」配方等
。不過大豆異黃酮在人體研究中，
攝取大豆異黃酮未提高子宮肌瘤、乳癌的發生風險
。比較需要留意的是 DHEA 這類荷爾蒙前驅物，或成分不清楚的配方。

**為什麼時間上會剛好對上？**

- 乳癌從開始形成到摸得到或驗得出來，通常需要好幾年，所以你吃膠原蛋白的那幾個月，腫瘤很可能早就存在了。
- 有些乳癌類型本來就長得比較快，例如 HER2 陽性或三陰性乳癌。就算沒吃任何保健品，腫瘤也可能在短時間內明顯變大。
- 兩件事時間接近，不代表一件事造成另一件事。這是很自然的聯想，但不一定是真正的原因。

1. 把當時吃的膠原蛋白產品包裝或成分表找出來，看看有沒有上面提到的添加物。
2. 帶去給你的腫瘤科醫師看，
讓醫師依個人狀況進行評估
。如果你的乳癌是荷爾蒙受體陽性（ER/PR+），醫師會特別在意你有沒有吃含荷爾蒙成分的東西。
3. 治療期間如果想吃任何保健食品，最好都先問過醫師。

I want to say this to you first: getting the diagnosis is hard enough already, and if you're blaming yourself because of this, you really don't need to. Based on current medical evidence, it is very unlikely that collagen itself is what gave you breast cancer or made the tumour grow.

**Collagen itself: currently no evidence that it causes cancer or makes tumours grow**

Family medicine physician Chen Hsin-mei says that
there is currently no credible medical evidence that "collagen itself causes breast cancer or endometrial cancer" or that it directly stimulates breast tumours; ingested collagen is digested and broken down into amino acids and small peptides, and does not go only to the breast or uterus and turn into tissue or lumps.
Material compiled by a dietitian also mentions that
even in observational epidemiological research, no literature has indicated that collagen raises the risk of developing or worsening breast cancer or uterine fibroids
.

**What you really need to watch out for is the other ingredients added to the product**

When doctors ask in clinic "have you been taking collagen?",
it is not about collagen itself, but about "estrogen-like additives" among the ingredients.
Some products may additionally contain
soy isoflavones (phytoestrogen), red clover (Red clover), placenta-related extracts, DHEA (a hormone precursor), or other vaguely labelled "women's conditioning / breast enhancement" formulas, etc.
. However, in human studies of soy isoflavones,
intake of soy isoflavones did not raise the risk of uterine fibroids or breast cancer
. What deserves more attention are hormone precursors like DHEA, or formulas with unclear ingredients.

**Why does the timing happen to line up?**

- Breast cancer usually takes several years from when it starts forming until it can be felt or detected, so the tumour very likely already existed during the months you were taking collagen.
- Some types of breast cancer naturally grow faster, such as HER2-positive or triple-negative breast cancer. Even without taking any supplements, a tumour can grow noticeably in a short time.
- Two things happening close together in time does not mean one caused the other. It's a very natural association to make, but it isn't necessarily the real cause.

**Here's what I suggest you can do**

1. Find the packaging or ingredient list of the collagen product you were taking at the time, and see whether it contains any of the additives mentioned above.
2. Take it to your oncologist,
so the doctor can assess it based on your individual situation
. If your breast cancer is hormone receptor-positive (ER/PR+), the doctor will be especially concerned about whether you have taken anything containing hormonal ingredients.
3. If you want to take any health supplements during treatment, it's best to ask your doctor first.

If you'd like, you can tell me the ingredients of that product, or your type of breast cancer, and I can help you see which points are worth asking your doctor about.

.

   我知道研究常提到癌症周圍的基質、纖維母細胞、膠原沉積與轉移有關，但這不能直接等同於「吃膠原蛋白會促進癌症」。

4. **癌症病人使用保健品要先問醫師。**  
   因為有些補充品可能影響治療、凝血、肝腎代謝，或和化療、標靶、荷爾蒙治療、放療產生交互作用。

但我也知道這是醫療與營養補充品問題，資訊可能更新，所以我剛才有搜尋確認。

---

## 二、我剛才查到的主要來源

### 1. Oncology Nursing Society：目前沒有證據顯示膠原補充品會影響腫瘤膠原、癌症進展或治療反應

我最直接依據的是 **Oncology Nursing Society, ONS** 2026 年的文章〈What the Evidence Says About Collagen for Patients With Cancer〉。它特別區分了「人體腫瘤微環境中的膠原」與「口服水解膠原蛋白補充品」。文章提到，雖然某些人體自身產生的膠原，例如 type XII collagen，可能和乳癌轉移或復發風險有關；但**目前沒有證據顯示膠原補充品會影響腫瘤內膠原含量、癌症進展或治療反應**。這是我回答「不能直接判定膠原蛋白讓腫瘤快速變大」的主要依據。([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))

### 2. National Cancer Institute：沒有證據證明任何保健品可治癌、防復發；癌症病人用補充品應與醫療團隊討論

美國 **National Cancer Institute, NCI** 的資料說明，目前沒有證據證明任何特殊飲食、食物、維生素、礦物質、草本或膳食補充品可以減緩癌症、治癒癌症或防止復發；同時也提醒癌症患者若使用輔助或替代療法，應與醫師或護理師討論。這支持我說「治療期間不要自行加保健品，應先問主治醫師」。([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/diets-supplements))

### 3. NCI：食物與膳食補充品可能和癌症治療互相影響

NCI 另有關於「癌症治療與食物／膳食補充品交互作用」的資料。它提到某些補充品可能影響治療，癌症患者應告知醫師自己正在使用的膳食補充品。這是我建議你把膠原蛋白瓶子、成分表拿給腫瘤科醫師看的理由。([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/patient/dietary-interactions-pdq))

### 4. American Cancer Society：不建議用膳食補充品來預防癌症

**American Cancer Society, ACS** 的營養與活動指南提到，雖然富含蔬菜、水果、植物性食物的飲食可能降低癌症風險，但膳食補充品沒有一致證據可達到同樣效果；ACS 目前不建議使用膳食補充品來預防癌症。這支持我對保健品採取保守態度，而不是鼓勵依賴補充品。([cancer.org](https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/diet-physical-activity/acs-guidelines-nutrition-physical-activity-cancer-prevention.html?cm_ven=ExactTarget))

### 5. 關於乳癌生長速度：系統性回顧指出乳癌倍增時間差異大，快慢與亞型有關

我查到一篇乳癌腫瘤倍增時間的系統性回顧。它指出，乳癌的腫瘤倍增時間在不同研究中差異很大；文中也提到較快生長的腫瘤常見於 grade 3、HER2 陽性、三陰性或 Ki-67 高的乳癌。這是我說「幾個月內變大可能是腫瘤本身生物特性」的依據。([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34264009/))

### 6. 另一篇研究：三陰性乳癌比 ER+/HER2- 乳癌有較短倍增時間

我也查到一篇以超音波追蹤診斷到手術期間腫瘤大小變化的研究。它發現三陰性乳癌的體積增加較多，倍增時間也比 ER 陽性／HER2 陰性乳癌短。這支持「某些乳癌亞型本來就可能長得較快」這一點。([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30259332/))

### 7. FDA：膳食補充品上市前通常不需由 FDA 審查安全性與有效性

美國 FDA 說明，FDA 沒有權限在膳食補充品上市前審查其安全性與有效性。這是我提醒「補充品品質、標示、添加成分要小心」的依據。([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/food/dietary-supplements/information-consumers-using-dietary-supplements))

---

## 三、我如何從這些來源推論到剛才的回答

我的邏輯是：

- 有研究顯示**腫瘤自身或腫瘤微環境中的膠原**可能和乳癌侵襲、轉移、復發有關。  
- 但目前沒有證據證明**口服膠原蛋白補充品**會讓腫瘤中的膠原增加，或讓乳癌進展更快。([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))  
- 乳癌快速變大，更常見、也更有醫學依據的解釋，是腫瘤本身的亞型與增殖速度，例如三陰性、HER2 陽性、高 grade、高 Ki-67。([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8335823/))  
- 因為補充品可能有其他添加物或與治療互相影響，所以即使不能說膠原蛋白害你腫瘤變大，也仍然應該把產品成分交給腫瘤科醫師確認。([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/patient/dietary-interactions-pdq))

所以我才會說：**目前證據不支持「吃幾個月膠原蛋白導致乳癌快速變大」這個結論；比較可能要從乳癌的 ER/PR、HER2、Ki-67、grade 等病理特徵去解釋。**

## 四、我不敢說什麼

我不能說「膠原蛋白絕對完全無風險」，因為：

- 不同產品成分不同；
- 有些產品可能不只含膠原蛋白，還有草本、胎盤、雌激素樣成分、抗氧化劑或其他添加物；
- 癌症治療期間，補充品可能和藥物或治療互相影響；
- 「沒有證據證明會促進腫瘤」不等於「已經證明對所有乳癌患者都絕對安全」。

因此最穩妥的做法是：**先停用，帶成分表問你的腫瘤科醫師或癌症營養師。**

A hug for you first. **Based on current evidence, "having taken collagen for a few months" cannot be directly judged to be the cause of the breast cancer growing quickly**; if it is ordinary hydrolysed collagen / collagen peptides, there is currently no clinical evidence showing that it increases collagen within tumours, accelerates cancer progression or affects treatment response. Online, "collagen in the tumour microenvironment" and "oral collagen supplements" are often lumped together, but these two are not the same thing. ([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer?utm_source=openai))

When breast cancer grows within a few months, the common reason is in fact **the biological characteristics of the tumour itself**, such as triple-negative, HER2-positive, high tumour grade, high Ki-67, etc.; these types can naturally grow faster. Studies also show that breast cancer doubling times vary widely, and faster-growing subtypes do exist. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8335823/?utm_source=openai)) In addition, a lump that feels like it "suddenly got bigger" may also be affected by measurement methods, inflammation and swelling, the menstrual cycle, and differences between imaging and palpation; it doesn't necessarily mean a particular food or supplement caused it.

But I would suggest you do the following:

1. **Don't blame yourself.** Breast cancer usually does not form or rapidly worsen because of taking a particular supplement for a few months; "it happened to come first in time" is not the same as "it caused the result".  
2. **Show the collagen bottle or ingredient list to your oncologist.** In particular, check whether it contains other additives, such as herbal, placental or hormone-related ingredients, high-dose vitamins, antioxidants, etc.  
3. **Don't add supplements on your own during treatment for now.** The US National Cancer Institute and NCCIH both recommend that cancer patients discuss any dietary supplement with their medical team before using it, because some supplements may interfere with treatment or pose risks. ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam?redirect=true&utm_source=openai))  
4. **Be careful about quality when choosing supplements.** Dietary supplements usually do not need FDA approval of their safety and effectiveness before going on the market the way drugs do, so quality and labelling may differ between brands. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/food/dietary-supplements/information-consumers-using-dietary-supplements?utm_source=openai))

Simply put: **there is currently no reliable evidence supporting "collagen made the breast cancer grow quickly"; it is more likely caused by the tumour's own subtype and proliferation rate.** But since you have already been diagnosed with breast cancer, it's best to have your attending doctor confirm any supplement before you take it. You can also ask your doctor what the **ER/PR, HER2, Ki-67 and Grade** in your report are; these explain why the tumour is growing fast better than collagen does.

My answer just now was based on two parts: **medical common knowledge I already had** + **information I just found through a real-time search**. Let me explain the two separately and clearly.

## 1. What I already knew before searching

Before searching, what I already knew were these "broad principles":

1. **Oral collagen is not intact collagen going straight into the tumour.**  
   Ordinary collagen supplements are mostly hydrolysed collagen or collagen peptides; after entering the gastrointestinal tract they are broken down into amino acids and small peptides and then used by the body. So you can't directly infer "eating collagen = adding collagen to the tumour = making the tumour grow".

2. **Breast cancer growth rates naturally vary a great deal.**  
   Some breast cancers grow slowly, others quickly; triple-negative, HER2-positive, high-grade and high-Ki-67 tumours usually proliferate faster.

3. **"Collagen in the tumour microenvironment" and "oral collagen supplements" are not the same thing.**  
   I know that research often mentions that the stroma, fibroblasts and collagen deposition around cancer are linked to metastasis, but this cannot be directly equated with "eating collagen promotes cancer".

4. **Cancer patients should ask their doctor before using supplements.**  
   Because some supplements may affect treatment, blood clotting, or liver and kidney metabolism, or interact with chemotherapy, targeted therapy, hormone therapy or radiotherapy.

But I also know this is a question about medicine and nutritional supplements, and the information may have been updated, so I did a search just now to confirm.

---

## 2. The main sources I just found

### 1. Oncology Nursing Society: currently no evidence that collagen supplements affect tumour collagen, cancer progression or treatment response

What I relied on most directly is the **Oncology Nursing Society, ONS** 2026 article "What the Evidence Says About Collagen for Patients With Cancer". It specifically distinguishes between "collagen in the human tumour microenvironment" and "oral hydrolysed collagen supplements". The article mentions that although certain collagen produced by the body itself, such as type XII collagen, may be linked to breast cancer metastasis or recurrence risk, **there is currently no evidence that collagen supplements affect tumour collagen content, cancer progression or treatment response**. This is the main basis for my answer that "it cannot be directly judged that collagen made the tumour grow quickly". ([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))

### 2. National Cancer Institute: no evidence that any supplement can cure cancer or prevent recurrence; cancer patients using supplements should discuss it with their medical team

Material from the US **National Cancer Institute, NCI** explains that there is currently no evidence that any special diet, food, vitamin, mineral, herb or dietary supplement can slow cancer, cure cancer or prevent recurrence; it also reminds cancer patients who use complementary or alternative therapies to discuss them with their doctor or nurse. This supports what I said: "don't add supplements on your own during treatment; ask your attending doctor first". ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/diets-supplements))

### 3. NCI: food and dietary supplements may interact with cancer treatment

The NCI also has material on "interactions between cancer treatment and food / dietary supplements". It mentions that some supplements may affect treatment and that cancer patients should tell their doctor which dietary supplements they are using. This is why I suggested you show the collagen bottle and ingredient list to your oncologist. ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/patient/dietary-interactions-pdq))

### 4. American Cancer Society: does not recommend using dietary supplements to prevent cancer

The **American Cancer Society, ACS** guideline on nutrition and physical activity mentions that although a diet rich in vegetables, fruit and plant foods may lower cancer risk, there is no consistent evidence that dietary supplements can achieve the same effect; the ACS currently does not recommend using dietary supplements to prevent cancer. This supports my cautious stance on supplements, rather than encouraging reliance on them. ([cancer.org](https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/diet-physical-activity/acs-guidelines-nutrition-physical-activity-cancer-prevention.html?cm_ven=ExactTarget))

### 5. On breast cancer growth rates: a systematic review indicates that breast cancer doubling times vary widely, and speed is related to subtype

I found a systematic review of breast cancer tumour doubling times. It points out that breast cancer tumour doubling times vary widely across studies; it also mentions that faster-growing tumours are common in grade 3, HER2-positive, triple-negative or high-Ki-67 breast cancers. This is the basis for my saying that "growth within a few months may be due to the tumour's own biological characteristics". ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34264009/))

### 6. Another study: triple-negative breast cancer has a shorter doubling time than ER+/HER2- breast cancer

I also found a study that used ultrasound to track changes in tumour size between diagnosis and surgery. It found that triple-negative breast cancers increased more in volume and also had shorter doubling times than ER-positive / HER2-negative breast cancers. This supports the point that "certain breast cancer subtypes can naturally grow faster". ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30259332/))

### 7. FDA: dietary supplements usually do not need FDA review of safety and effectiveness before going on the market

The US FDA explains that the FDA does not have the authority to review dietary supplements for safety and effectiveness before they are marketed. This is the basis for my caution that "you need to be careful about supplement quality, labelling and added ingredients". ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/food/dietary-supplements/information-consumers-using-dietary-supplements))

---

## 3. How I reasoned from these sources to my answer just now

My logic is:

- Research shows that **collagen of the tumour itself or in the tumour microenvironment** may be linked to breast cancer invasion, metastasis and recurrence.  
- But there is currently no evidence that **oral collagen supplements** increase collagen in tumours or make breast cancer progress faster. ([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))  
- For rapid breast cancer growth, the more common and more medically grounded explanation is the tumour's own subtype and proliferation rate, such as triple-negative, HER2-positive, high grade, high Ki-67. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8335823/))  
- Because supplements may contain other additives or interact with treatment, even if we can't say collagen made your tumour grow, you should still give the product's ingredients to your oncologist to confirm. ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/patient/dietary-interactions-pdq))

That's why I said: **current evidence does not support the conclusion that "taking collagen for a few months caused the breast cancer to grow quickly"; it is more likely to be explained by pathological features of the breast cancer such as ER/PR, HER2, Ki-67 and grade.**

## 4. What I don't dare to say

I can't say "collagen is absolutely and completely risk-free", because:

- different products have different ingredients;
- some products may contain not only collagen but also herbal, placental or estrogen-like ingredients, antioxidants or other additives;
- during cancer treatment, supplements may interact with drugs or treatment;
- "no evidence that it promotes tumours" is not the same as "already proven absolutely safe for all breast cancer patients".

So the safest approach is: **stop taking it for now, and bring the ingredient list to ask your oncologist or oncology dietitian.**

### 2. Oncology Nursing Society：What the Evidence Says About Collagen for Patients With Cancer

這篇是腫瘤護理相關來源，直接討論「癌症病人與膠原蛋白補充品」。它的重點非常貼近你的問題：雖然水解膠原胜肽可能增加皮膚或結締組織中的膠原生成，但**目前沒有證據顯示膠原蛋白補充品會影響腫瘤中的膠原含量、癌症進展或治療反應**。它也建議腫瘤護理人員要詢問病人是否使用膠原蛋白，並鼓勵病人和癌症照護團隊討論。([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))

這是我回答你「目前不能說吃膠原蛋白導致腫瘤快速變大」的重要依據之一，因為它直接把**口服補充品**和**癌症進展**分開說明。([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))

### 3. National Cancer Institute：Popular Diets, Supplements, and Cancer

美國國家癌症研究所 NCI 對癌症病人使用飲食與補充品的說法是：沒有證據證明某種營養趨勢、食物、維生素、礦物質、保健品或草藥可以減緩、治癒癌症，或防止癌症復發；同時也提醒病人在使用任何補充品前要告訴醫師、護理師或營養師，因為某些補充品可能有風險或影響治療。([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/diets-supplements))

### 4. NCI：Cancer Therapy Interactions With Foods and Dietary Supplements

我的推論分成三層：

### 第一層：有沒有直接證據？

我找到的可靠來源並沒有說「口服膠原蛋白會造成乳癌快速長大」。相反地，Oncology Nursing Society 明確指出，目前沒有證據顯示膠原補充品會影響腫瘤膠原含量、癌症進展或治療反應。([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))

所以，我不能說「這是真的」。

### 第二層：有沒有理論上的疑慮？

有。MSK 提到，膠原蛋白在癌症中有複雜、雙向的角色；某些研究看到高膠原環境可能促進乳癌模型中的轉移，也有研究看到相反或保護性結果。([mskcc.org](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/collagen))

所以，我也不能說「完全不用管、絕對沒關係」。比較準確的說法是：**理論和前臨床研究還在釐清，但目前沒有足夠人類臨床證據證明口服膠原蛋白讓乳癌快速長大。**

### 第三層：臨床上該怎麼做？

因為你已經確診乳癌，最安全的做法是把你吃過的產品拿給主治醫師看，尤其要確認它是否只含膠原蛋白，還是另有維他命、草本、胎盤素、蜂王乳、異黃酮、DHEA、荷爾蒙相關成分或不明胜肽。NCI 和 ACS 都建議癌症病人使用保健品前應與醫療團隊討論，因為補充品可能影響治療或有安全性問題。([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/diets-supplements))

---

## 總結一句話

我不是因為「直覺覺得不會」，而是因為目前可靠來源顯示：**腫瘤微環境中的膠原蛋白確實可能和乳癌行為有關，但目前沒有證據證明口服膠原蛋白補充品會讓乳癌快速變大。**不過，因為你已經確診，任何保健品都應該讓腫瘤科醫師確認，尤其要看完整成分，而不只看產品正面寫的「膠原蛋白」。

A hug for you first. **Judging by the medical evidence currently available, it cannot be said that "taking collagen for a few months caused the breast cancer to grow quickly" is true**. The sequence of events you noticed is very frightening, but "the tumour grew after taking collagen" and "collagen caused the tumour to grow" are two different things; there is currently **no clinical evidence proving that oral collagen supplements make breast cancer grow faster, worsen or recur**. The more common reason for a tumour growing quickly is the biological characteristics of the tumour itself, such as subtype, grade, HER2/triple-negative status, Ki-67 proliferation index, hormone receptor status, etc.

What is easy to confuse is this: research often mentions that "collagen in the tumour microenvironment" may be linked to cancer cell invasion, metastasis or treatment response; but that is **collagen structure formed by the body's own tissue / around the tumour**, which does not mean that the collagen powder you eat goes directly to feed the tumour. Oral collagen is usually broken down in the digestive tract into amino acids or small peptides before being absorbed. Memorial Sloan Kettering points out that collagen's role in cancer is complex, with animal or laboratory studies showing both promoting and inhibiting effects, and more research is still needed; the Oncology Nursing Society also points out that there is currently no evidence that collagen supplements affect tumour collagen content, cancer progression or treatment response. ([mskcc.org](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/collagen?utm_source=openai))

However, I would suggest you do these few things now:

1. **Take the brand, ingredient list, dose, and start and stop dates of the collagen you took to your breast surgeon / oncologist.**  
   Some products are not pure collagen and may also contain high-dose vitamins, herbs, estrogen-like ingredients, placenta extract, peptides, ingredients with hormone-related claims, etc.; these are the ones that more need to be checked one by one.

2. **During treatment, don't keep taking any supplement on your own unless your attending doctor or oncology dietitian agrees.**  
   The US National Cancer Institute reminds cancer patients to tell their medical team before using dietary supplements, because some supplements may affect treatment or have safety issues. ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/diets-supplements?utm_source=openai))

3. **Ask your doctor: "Why does my tumour seem to be growing so fast?"**  
   You can ask your doctor to explain:  
   - ER / PR / HER2 status  
   - Ki-67  
   - tumour grade  
   - whether the imaging and pathology sizes are consistent  
   - whether there is inflammation, swelling, bleeding or measurement differences  
   These usually explain the speed of tumour growth better than "having taken collagen".

4. **Don't blame yourself.**  
   Breast cancer usually forms as the result of many factors over a long time; a few months of collagen supplementation can hardly be considered the single cause. The most important thing for you now is to get clear on your subtype, stage and treatment plan, and to receive treatment on schedule.

Simply put: **there is currently no evidence supporting "collagen made your breast cancer grow quickly"; but after a diagnosis, any supplement should be stopped first, or at least shown to your oncologist for confirmation.**

Because this involves breast cancer and supplement safety, I didn't rely on memory alone, but searched for more reliable sources from cancer institutions / oncology care.

## What I already knew before searching

Before searching, what I already knew were these "general principles of medicine and biology":

1. **Oral collagen is not whole collagen going directly into the tumour.**  
   Collagen is a protein; after it is eaten it is usually broken down in the digestive tract into amino acids or small peptides and then absorbed and used by the body. This is also why from the start I wouldn't directly infer "eating collagen = feeding the tumour".

2. **The "collagen" mentioned in cancer research often refers to collagen in the tumour microenvironment.**  
   The stroma, fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and collagen alignment and density around breast cancer really may affect cancer cell invasion, immune cell entry, metastasis risk or treatment response. But this does not mean oral collagen supplements have been proven to have the same effect.

3. **Rapid breast cancer growth is usually more often related to the biological characteristics of the tumour itself.**  
   For example ER/PR/HER2 status, Ki-67, tumour grade, triple-negative breast cancer, HER2-positive breast cancer, local inflammation or differences in imaging measurement. These usually explain tumour growth rate better than "a particular ordinary supplement".

4. **Cancer patients should be careful with supplements, but "be careful" does not mean "proven to promote cancer".**  
   I already knew that many cancer centres advise patients to tell their medical team about all supplements, because of possible problems with interactions, inconsistent quality, unclear doses or other added ingredients.

The above was my basic judgement before searching. But because what you asked is a specific and high-risk question — "could collagen make breast cancer grow quickly" — I looked up information again to confirm.

---

## The main sources I relied on just now

### 1. Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center: Collagen entry

This is one of the main sources I referred to, because Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, MSK, is a major cancer centre, and its About Herbs database is often used to assess the safety of herbs and supplements used by cancer patients. MSK's take on collagen is: collagen supplements are often claimed to improve skin, nails, joints, etc., but in the context of cancer, the research findings are complex; laboratory or animal studies show that collagen may play a dual role in cancer, with some studies showing that a high-collagen environment may promote breast cancer metastasis models and others showing tumour-suppressing effects, so more research is still needed to clarify this. ([mskcc.org](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/collagen))

The key point I took from this source is: **it can't be simplified to "collagen definitely promotes cancer" or "it is definitely safe and irrelevant"; human clinical evidence is currently insufficient, and in particular, collagen in the tumour microenvironment cannot be directly equated with oral collagen supplements.**([mskcc.org](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/collagen))

---

### 2. Oncology Nursing Society: What the Evidence Says About Collagen for Patients With Cancer

This is an oncology nursing source that directly discusses "cancer patients and collagen supplements". Its main points are very close to your question: although hydrolysed collagen peptides may increase collagen production in skin or connective tissue, **there is currently no evidence that collagen supplements affect collagen content in tumours, cancer progression or treatment response**. It also advises oncology nurses to ask patients whether they use collagen, and encourages patients to discuss it with their cancer care team. ([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))

This is one of the important bases for my answer that "it currently can't be said that taking collagen caused the tumour to grow quickly", because it directly separates **oral supplements** and **cancer progression**. ([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))

---

### 3. National Cancer Institute: Popular Diets, Supplements, and Cancer

The US National Cancer Institute, NCI, says about cancer patients' use of diets and supplements: there is no evidence that any nutrition trend, food, vitamin, mineral, health supplement or herbal remedy can slow or cure cancer, or prevent cancer recurrence; it also reminds patients to tell their doctor, nurse or dietitian before using any supplement, because some supplements may carry risks or affect treatment. ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/diets-supplements))

What I use this source to support is not "collagen is definitely harmful", but this recommendation: **after diagnosis, don't continue using supplements on your own; show the product ingredients to your oncologist or dietitian for confirmation.**([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/diets-supplements))

---

### 4. NCI: Cancer Therapy Interactions With Foods and Dietary Supplements

This is NCI material on interactions between food, supplements and cancer treatment. It cautions that during cancer treatment some supplements may interact with treatment, so it is necessary to discuss them with the medical team. ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/patient/dietary-interactions-pdq))

Based on this source, I remind you: even though there is currently no evidence that collagen makes breast cancer grow quickly, **during treatment you should still tell your medical team about all supplements, herbal remedies, vitamins, protein powders, etc.** ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/patient/dietary-interactions-pdq))

---

### 5. American Cancer Society: How to Use Integrative Therapies Safely

The American Cancer Society cautions that if cancer patients use integrative therapies or dietary supplements, they should ask their cancer care team about the risks, the benefits and whether they will interact with standard treatment, and they should not rely on over-the-counter products to treat cancer or serious illnesses. ([cancer.org](https://www.cancer.org/cancer/supportive-care/integrative-medicine/how-to-use-safely.html))

I use this source to support the point that "supplements should be disclosed openly to the medical team", not to say that collagen has been proven to promote cancer. ([cancer.org](https://www.cancer.org/cancer/supportive-care/integrative-medicine/how-to-use-safely.html))

---

### 6. MSK: Reality Check: What You Should Know About Peptides and Cancer

This article is not simply about collagen, but about the "peptide / peptides" products that have become popular in recent years. MSK's breast cancer oncologist cautions that many wellness peptides sold online lack rigorous clinical trials and their quality and long-term safety are questionable; cancer patients should be especially careful, because the effects on tumours of some products claimed to promote repair or reduce inflammation may be unknown. ([mskcc.org](https://www.mskcc.org/news/reality-check-what-you-should-know-about-peptides-and))

My intention in citing this source is: if the product you took is just plain "hydrolysed collagen", that's one thing; but if the product also has various "peptides", "anti-ageing", "repair", "hormone balance" or other ingredients added, more caution is needed. ([mskcc.org](https://www.mskcc.org/news/reality-check-what-you-should-know-about-peptides-and))

---

## How did I reason in the end?

My reasoning has three layers:

### Layer one: is there direct evidence?

The reliable sources I found do not say that "oral collagen causes breast cancer to grow quickly". On the contrary, the Oncology Nursing Society clearly states that there is currently no evidence that collagen supplements affect tumour collagen content, cancer progression or treatment response. ([ons.org](https://www.ons.org/publications-research/voice/news-views/03-2026/what-evidence-says-about-collagen-patients-cancer))

So I can't say "this is true".

### Layer two: are there theoretical concerns?

Yes. MSK mentions that collagen plays a complex, two-way role in cancer; some studies have seen that a high-collagen environment may promote metastasis in breast cancer models, while other studies have seen opposite or protective results. ([mskcc.org](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/collagen))

So I also can't say "you don't need to worry about it at all, it's absolutely fine". The more accurate way to put it is: **the theory and preclinical research are still being clarified, but there is currently not enough human clinical evidence to prove that oral collagen makes breast cancer grow quickly.**

### Layer three: what should be done clinically?

Because you have already been diagnosed with breast cancer, the safest approach is to show the products you took to your attending doctor, in particular to confirm whether they contain only collagen, or also vitamins, herbs, placenta extract, royal jelly, isoflavones, DHEA, hormone-related ingredients or unidentified peptides. Both the NCI and the ACS recommend that cancer patients discuss supplements with their medical team before using them, because supplements may affect treatment or have safety issues. ([cancer.gov](https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/treatment/cam/diets-supplements))

---

## Summary in one sentence

It's not because I "intuitively feel it wouldn't", but because current reliable sources show that: **collagen in the tumour microenvironment may indeed be linked to breast cancer behaviour, but there is currently no evidence that oral collagen supplements make breast cancer grow quickly.**However, since you have already been diagnosed, any supplement should be confirmed by your oncologist, and in particular you should look at the full ingredient list, not just the "collagen" written on the front of the product.
