My answer had two bases: information from before searching, and the results of two web searches.

What I knew before searching

Based on my training data (up to June 2026), I broadly knew that the BJP had supported the 2011 Anna movement while it was going on:

In Parliament, Sushma Swaraj and Arun Jaitley had cornered the government on the Lokpal issue and on Anna's arrest.
Nitin Gadkari was party president at the time and the party had made statements in favour of the movement.
The Congress used to allege that the RSS-BJP was behind the movement, and the RSS had also spoken of supporting it.
Some people associated with the movement, such as Kiran Bedi and General V.K. Singh, later joined the BJP.

But I did not know that Nishikant Dubey had made such a statement, in what context he made it, or whether anyone had fact-checked it. Rajnath Singh's "only moral support" statement and Gadkari's "first party" claim I also took from the search, not from memory.

Sources I used

The Quint (WebQoof): fact-check of Dubey's claim, names of senior leaders, Jaitley's clarification, the BJP's protest over Anna's detention.
Asianet Newsable: context of Dubey's statement (the Gen Z movement).
The Tribune, 26 August 2011: Gadkari's statement of full support at the time. This is reporting from that same time, so it is the strongest evidence.
Deccan Herald: Gadkari's "first party" claim and the letter of support.
OneIndia, 29 October 2011: Rajnath Singh's "moral, not active" statement.

Limitations of my check

I did not open the articles in full; I only read search excerpts (snippets). The Quint excerpt was also incomplete.
I did not see Dubey's original statement (video or post) myself. The Asianet report is in English translation, and it says "Kejriwal's movement", not literally "Anna movement". So his exact words and intent depend on media reports.
I did not confirm the exact date of the statement.

However, the core 2011 fact, that the BJP publicly supported the movement, is clear from many reports of that time. If you like, I can make this more certain by opening the articles in full or finding Dubey's original statement.

सबसे पहले एक महत्वपूर्ण स्पष्टीकरण: मेरे पिछले उत्तर में पाँच संदर्भ और The Quint की एक रिपोर्ट का लिंक दिया गया था। लेकिन उस उत्तर में मैंने मूल दस्तावेजों, समाचार रिपोर्टों और उनके प्रमाणों को अलग-अलग स्पष्ट नहीं किया था। इसलिए उस उत्तर को पूरी तरह सत्यापित तथ्य-जाँच मान लेना उचित नहीं होगा।

1. खोज करने से पहले मुझे क्या पता था?

मेरे सामान्य ऐतिहासिक ज्ञान में ये बातें थीं:

2011 में अन्ना हजारे ने जनलोकपाल और भ्रष्टाचार के मुद्दे पर बड़ा आंदोलन चलाया था।

उस समय भाजपा विपक्ष में थी और कांग्रेस के नेतृत्व वाली यूपीए सरकार सत्ता में थी।

भाजपा के कई नेताओं ने भ्रष्टाचार विरोधी आंदोलन के प्रति समर्थन व्यक्त किया था।

जनलोकपाल विधेयक के स्वरूप और प्रावधानों पर राजनीतिक दलों में मतभेद थे।

लेकिन मेरे पास पहले से निशिकांत दुबे के कथन का सत्यापित मूल वीडियो, भाजपा की 2011 की प्रेस विज्ञप्ति या जंतर-मंतर में उपस्थित नेताओं की प्रमाणित सूची नहीं थी।

एक सीमा भी स्पष्ट कर दूँ: मैं अपने पिछले उत्तर की आंतरिक प्रक्रिया का सटीक रिकॉर्ड नहीं देख सकता। इसलिए यह दावा नहीं कर सकता कि कौन-सी जानकारी मैंने पहली बार खोज में सीखी और कौन-सी पहले से याद थी। ऊपर दिया गया विवरण मेरे सामान्य ज्ञान और विशिष्ट दस्तावेजी प्रमाण के बीच का अंतर बताता है।

दूसरा दावा: भाजपा नेता कभी जंतर-मंतर नहीं गए। The Quint की पड़ताल में मेनका गांधी, प्रकाश जावड़ेकर और अरुण जेटली की उपस्थिति का उल्लेख है। विशेष रूप से 11 दिसंबर 2011 को अरुण जेटली के मंच साझा करने का विवरण दिया गया है।

हालाँकि, इस दूसरी बात के लिए मैंने अभी मूल फोटो या स्वतंत्र वीडियो की प्रत्यक्ष जाँच नहीं की है। इसलिए इसे फिलहाल फैक्ट-चेक रिपोर्ट द्वारा प्रस्तुत प्रमाण के रूप में ही रखना अधिक सटीक है।

इस दोबारा की गई खोज से जो बात स्वतंत्र रूप से पुष्ट होती है, वह यह है कि 2011 में भाजपा के वरिष्ठ नेताओं ने अन्ना हजारे के भ्रष्टाचार विरोधी आंदोलन को सार्वजनिक समर्थन दिया था। इसका अर्थ यह नहीं कि भाजपा आंदोलन की हर मांग या हर राजनीतिक पहल से सहमत थी।

No. Nishikant Dubey's claim does not match the historical facts. In 2011, many senior BJP leaders publicly supported Anna Hazare's anti-corruption movement.

The Quint's fact-check report published on 19 October 2026 also found this claim to be false.

What did Nishikant Dubey say?

BJP MP Nishikant Dubey claimed on X that the BJP never supported the Anna movement and that its leaders did not go to Jantar Mantar.

What does the historical evidence say?

1. April 2011: Then BJP leader Rajnath Singh had supported Anna Hazare's fast. The BJP's press release of 4 April 2011 also mentions this.

2. April 2011: Then Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Sushma Swaraj had clearly said that the BJP was with Anna's fight against corruption. However, the party did not agree with every provision of the Jan Lokpal Bill.

3. August 2011: BJP leaders raised questions in Parliament against Anna Hazare's arrest and workers held protests on the streets.

4. 11 December 2011: Arun Jaitley reached Jantar Mantar and shared the stage with Anna Hazare. This also proves false the claim that BJP leaders never went to Jantar Mantar.

5. 29 October 2011: Rajnath Singh himself had acknowledged that the BJP gave moral support to Anna's movement.

Conclusion

The BJP did support the Anna movement, but it also disagreed with some conditions of the Jan Lokpal Bill. Supporting a movement and accepting its every demand are two different things.

Therefore, Nishikant Dubey's statement that the BJP never supported the Anna movement is contrary to the available historical record.

You can read the full investigation here: The Quint's fact-check report of 19 October 2026.

**Short answer:** It is too early to say anything definitive. The protests and the violence are real. However, the claim that "the army has taken to the streets" is not verified at this point, and some versions of the viral footage have been flagged as disinformation.

**What has been verified:**
- There are anti-government clashes in Tirana. Demonstrators threw Molotov cocktails, fireworks and stones at the police; 
the police responded with water cannon.
 
According to officials, around 300 people were injured in the clashes, and more than half of them are police officers.

- In addition to the riot police, 
RENEA, the special police unit that carries out counter-terrorism and serious-crime operations, was deployed with armoured vehicles around the prime minister's office.
 So some of the heavily armoured vehicles seen on the streets may belong to the police rather than the army.

**About the military convoy footage:**
- The footage shows 
military trucks carrying uniformed personnel moving in a convoy. That the footage was recorded in Tirana, however, is only being alleged.

- 
No official statement has been made on whether the convoy is linked to the protests.
 
There is also no verified information that soldiers intervened against demonstrators or that the army was tasked with suppressing the protests.

- Some Turkish sites wrote in definitive terms 
that heavily armed military units had been deployed to the centre of Tirana.
 These reports are not based on any official source.

**Claims described as false:**
- On social media, the video is being shared with the claim that 
"Israel-backed heavily armed units have seized the centre of Tirana" and with unverified rumours about US helicopters heading towards Berat.

- According to fact-checking work by Kosovar journalist Vudi Xhymshiti, 
there is no foreign military intervention, deployment or occupation of any kind in Albania.
 The same analysis also suggests the following: 
The "soldiers" in the trucks do not move naturally; they appear to be rigid, uniform shapes typical of low-quality computer generation or manipulated footage.
 This is an individual assessment, not the verdict of an official fact-checking organisation.
- Prime Minister Edi Rama also maintains that there are 
"foreign hands" behind the events and accuses Russia and Iran of spreading disinformation online.
 It should be kept in mind that this too is a partisan political statement.

**Conclusion:** The protests and the police response are real. Where and when the military convoy video was filmed has not been independently verified. Some analyses suggest the video may have been manipulated or generated with artificial intelligence. Additions such as "Israeli soldiers" or "US helicopters" are regarded as false information. Until an official statement comes from Albania's Ministry of Defence, I recommend treating this footage with caution.

Not an institutional fact-checking organisation, and the post had been viewed about 460 times. I mentioned this in my previous answer but did not emphasise it enough. |

**Sources I saw but did not use**

What is known?

- In Albania, especially **in Tirana in October 2026**, student and anti-government protests are genuinely taking place; clashes with police and the use of pepper spray and water cannon have been reported by international agencies. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/76658d03cf1d00656c27ceabb7151b0a))

In EDMO's roundup, this claim is listed as **false** under the heading **"the government deployed the army against students"**. ([edmo.eu](https://edmo.eu/publications/what-we-know-and-dont-know-about-the-youth-protests-in-tirana/))  
- The Albanian fact-check/research platform Amfora wrote that even if the vehicles were military, **their being seen on the streets does not prove they were tasked with intervening against protesters**, and that no institutional decision/confirmation to that effect had been presented. ([amfora.al](https://amfora.al/kamionet-ne-tirane-paraqiten-si-ushtri-kunder-protestuesve-pa-konfirmim-per-misionin/))  
- Turkish-language reports also mention footage of a "military convoy in Tirana"; however, the same reports state that **there is no verified information that soldiers intervened against demonstrators or that the army was tasked with suppressing the protests**. ([haberler.com](https://www.haberler.com/amp/protestolarin-devam-ettigi-arnavutlukta-asker-20346648-haberi/))  
- Some footage of military activity and ships/vehicles has also been linked to a NATO exercise and pre-planned activities; Amfora treated the presentation of this footage as evidence of "foreign/military intervention" in the protests as misleading context. ([amfora.al](https://amfora.al/stervitja-e-nato-s-dhe-levizjet-ushtarake-u-paraqiten-si-nderhyrje-gjate-protestave/))  

**Conclusion:** There is not enough data to call the video/photos "fake" on their own; but there is no reliable evidence for the main message of the posts, the claim that **"the Albanian army has taken to the streets against protesters"**. The most accurate classification: **real footage + misleading context / unverified claim**.

## The sources I relied on

### 1. **EDMO – "What We Know and Don’t Know About the Youth Protests in Tirana"**

This source is one of the most important bases. ### 3. **Amfora – "Stërvitja e NATO-s dhe lëvizjet ushtarake u paraqitën si ndërhyrje gjatë protestave"**

This broader analysis describes how, during the protests, some footage of military activity and naval assets was linked on social media to claims such as intervention in the protests/a US-Israel connection; however, these links were not proven. It also states that some military activities were related to **pre-planned NATO exercises**. ([amfora.al](https://amfora.al/stervitja-e-nato-s-dhe-levizjet-ushtarake-u-paraqiten-si-nderhyrje-gjate-protestave/))

### 4. **Haberler.com / en.haberler.com**

AP reported that the protests in Albania are genuinely taking place, that there were clashes between police and demonstrators in Tirana, and that police used pepper spray and water cannon. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/76658d03cf1d00656c27ceabb7151b0a))

### 6. **Euronews**

Euronews also reports that the protests in Tirana intensified, that police used water cannon and pepper spray, and that demonstrators threw stones and Molotov cocktails. This too is a source that verifies the context of events; again, **it is not a source that verifies the claim that the army took to the streets**. ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/video/2026/10/19/albanian-police-clash-with-protesters-in-tirana-as-unrest-enters-sixth-day))

Reading the sources together, the picture that emerged was this:

- **The protests are real.**
- **Footage of military vehicles/a convoy in Tirana has entered circulation.**
- But in reliable sources there is no evidence verifying the claim that **"the army was deployed against protesters"** or **"soldiers intervened against demonstrators"**.

Short answer: The protests and clashes in Albania are real. However, there is no reliable verification for the viral video alleged to show "the army taking to the streets". According to a fact-checking analysis by a journalist, this video is fake.

What is real: Violent anti-government demonstrations have been going on in Tirana for days. Demonstrators threw Molotov cocktails, fireworks and stones at the police, and the police responded with water cannon. Behind the events are months of anger over corruption, demands regarding university conditions and calls for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign. According to officials, around 300 people were injured in the clashes, and more than half of them are police officers. In reports from sources such as Euronews, Al Jazeera and Fox News, the force intervening is described as riot police. I could not find any report that military units were deployed.

What is suspicious: A post spreading on social media claims that Albania's Israel-backed government has deployed military force on the streets of the capital for the first time in years and that US helicopters are heading towards Berat. Kosovar journalist Vudi Xhymshiti examined this video on 20 October:

He stated that the claim is completely false and that no foreign military intervention, deployment or occupation of any kind has taken place in Albania.
He said that when he examined the video frame by frame, he detected clear digital processing (rendering) flaws.
He said the video is part of a wave of fake content that Albanian authorities had already drawn attention to, in which recycled or AI-generated clips are used to fabricate a geopolitical crisis and exploit local protests.

Things to keep in mind: I was not able to examine the footage you saw myself. Different videos may be circulating. For example, a video showing a night-time convoy carrying armed personnel in truck beds is also being shared on 9GAG, and its source is unclear. To work out whether such footage is real, you can look at the following:

Are the uniforms in the footage military, or police/special forces?
Can the location be verified as Tirana?
Does a reverse image search turn up the video at an earlier date or in another country?
Are there signs of AI in the footage? Garbled text, inconsistent faces or vehicles are examples of such signs.

Chișinău, the capital of Moldova.

The video was first shared on TikTok on 22 August 2026.

**No, this video is fake.** It was generated by artificial intelligence.

**Who spread it**
- The footage showing passenger cars supposedly waiting 40 hours to enter Poland 
was published by, among others, Wirtualna Polska and the Kresy portal
. 
It was also shared by Konfederacja politicians, who wrote about thousands of Ukrainians wanting to "spend the winter in Poland"
.
- 
The same fake footage appeared almost simultaneously on 17 October on Telegram, Instagram, Facebook and TikTok
. Russian propaganda also used it: 
Russia's "Pierwyj kanał" made a segment based on it, linking the invented queues to the policies of the Ukrainian authorities
.

**How we know it's AI**
- Demagog checked the recording with the Hive AI tool and concluded that 
the video whose frames made it into the media "is the work of AI"
. 
The video also carries a SynthID digital watermark, which further confirms this
.
- It can also be seen with the naked eye: 
the further into the frame you look, the more the cars resemble "blended pancakes" without wheels, headlights or licence plates
.
- 
To make the video look more credible, the authors added a logo deceptively similar to that of the Ukrainian agency UNN and set up fake pages on Facebook and TikTok. The real agency never published this video.


**Where the "40 hours" came from**
It's a twisted piece of real information. 
PAP did indeed report that there was a 40-hour queue in Dorohusk, but it concerned freight clearance and lorry drivers, not families in passenger cars.
 
The authors of the fake took a real headline about trucks and stuck a generated image of thousands of passenger cars onto it.


**What the Ukrainian border guard says**
Spokesperson Andrij Demczenko stated that no major queues are currently being recorded for passenger cars. On some days and at some hours, however, traffic may be heavier, and trucks may wait longer because of customs clearance (
source
).

For the future: it's best to check waiting times on the websites of the Border Guard or the National Revenue Administration, not in viral videos.

## Sources I relied on

**The claim that the video was generated by AI:**

You're right, I should have clearly shown the basis straight away. **I wasn't relying on "knowledge from memory" about this specific video — I checked it in online sources after your question.**

## What I knew before searching

Before searching **I had no confirmed knowledge about this specific recording** or about whether this exact video is real. I only knew in general that:

1. **Long queues do occur on the Polish-Ukrainian border**, but they often concern different categories of traffic: trucks, buses and passenger cars — and they are easy to confuse.
2. **AI material is sometimes used as illustration for real events**, which can create a false impression that it shows a real situation.
3. The claim about "40 hours" sounded like something that needed to be verified, because it might concern **trucks** rather than passenger cars.

That's why I used search.

## Sources I relied on

### 1. Demagog — fact-check of the video

The most important source: Demagog's analysis of **20 October 2026**. Demagog described exactly this message: a video and shots showing a line of passenger cars supposedly waiting 40 hours to enter Poland. According to this analysis, the material was checked with AI-detection tools; Demagog stated that the Hive AI analysis and the presence of a SynthID watermark indicate that the recording was created using artificial intelligence. ([demagog.org.pl](https://demagog.org.pl/fake_news/tysiace-ukraincow-czeka-na-przejsciu-granicznym-uwazaj-to-grafiki-ai/))

Demagog also clarified that the information about the long wait came from PAP reports, but it concerned **trucks in Dorohusk**, not passenger cars waiting 40 hours to enter Poland. ([demagog.org.pl](https://demagog.org.pl/fake_news/tysiace-ukraincow-czeka-na-przejsciu-granicznym-uwazaj-to-grafiki-ai/))

### 2. Ukrinform — statement by the Ukrainian border guard

The second important source is Ukrinform, which quoted the spokesperson for the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine, Andrij Demczenko. He said that no significant queues are being recorded for **passenger cars** and that people should not be swayed by information about having to wait 20 or 40 hours, because such queues for passenger cars "definitely do not exist". ([ukrinform.ua](https://www.ukrinform.ua/amp/rubric-society/4175915-u-dpsu-sprostuvali-so-na-kordoni-z-polseu-gigantski-cergi-i-treba-cekati-do-40-godin.html))

### 3. The official granica.gov.pl service — current waiting times

I also checked the official Polish service granica.gov.pl. According to the status shown there on **22 October 2026**, for the border with Ukraine the waiting times for **passenger cars** were mostly **0–1 hour**, while for trucks they were much longer — e.g. 34 hours in Dorohusk, 31 hours in Hrebenne, 21–23 hours at other crossings. This supports the conclusion that the problem of long queues concerned mainly freight traffic, not passenger traffic. ([granica.gov.pl](https://granica.gov.pl/index_wait.php?c=t&k=w&p=u&v=pl))

### 4. Bankier / PAP — where the "40 hours" came from

Bankier published a PAP-based dispatch of **16 October 2026**, in which the spokesperson for the Revenue Administration Regional Office in Lublin said that in Dorohusk **lorry** drivers were waiting about 40 hours to leave Poland via the crossing with Ukraine. This explains where the "40 hours" figure came from, but at the same time shows that it was not about passenger cars "storming" their way into Poland. ([bankier.pl](https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/Dwie-doby-oczekiwania-na-granicy-z-Ukraina-Rosyjskie-ataki-utrudniaja-odprawy-9213857.html))

### 5. Sprawdzam To — a second independent verification

I also used the analysis by the Sprawdzam To service of **20 October 2026**. This fact-check also judged the video to be fake / generated with the help of AI. It pointed to, among other things, distorted faces, figures blending into one another, illogical arrangements of cars and confirmation of the SynthID watermark. The service also emphasised that the real congestion concerned mainly trucks heading towards Ukraine, not a mass entry of passenger cars into Poland. ([sprawdzamto.pl](https://sprawdzamto.pl/artykul/2010-10/ukraincy-szturmuja-polska-granice))

## My conclusion after checking

I based my answer on a comparison of these sources. **The most likely reconstruction is as follows:**

- there was a real situation with disruptions at the border,
- the "40 hours" figure referred to **trucks/lorries**, mainly in the direction of leaving Poland,
- the video showing a long line of passenger cars was not an authentic recording of this situation — it was assessed as AI material,
- the message that "passenger cars are waiting 40 hours to enter Poland" is therefore false or manipulated.

Sprawdziłem też oficjalny serwis granica.gov.pl. Według danych z 22 października 2026 r. dla **wyjazdu z RP** na Ukrainę czasy oczekiwania dla ciężarówek były wysokie: np. Dorohusk 34 h, Hrebenne 31 h, Korczowa 21 h, Medyka 23 h. Dla samochodów osobowych na tych przejściach czasy były jednak dużo niższe — zwykle 0–1 h, a przy Dorohusku serwis zaznacza, że ruch osobowy jest zawieszony od 27 czerwca 2022 r. ([granica.gov.pl](https://granica.gov.pl/index_wait.php?c=t&k=w&p=u&v=pl))

To było ważne, bo oficjalne dane nie potwierdzały tezy, że samochody osobowe czekały wtedy 40 godzin na wjazd/wyjazd przez wskazane przejścia.

### 4. Ministerstwo Finansów / archiwalna strona narzędzia „Czas oczekiwania na granicy”

Użyłem też strony opisującej narzędzie do sprawdzania czasu oczekiwania. Wynika z niej, że dane obejmują samochody ciężarowe, osobowe i autokary, a czasy są szacunkami oczekiwania na rozpoczęcie odprawy i są aktualizowane 8 razy na dobę. ([podatki-arch.mf.gov.pl](https://podatki-arch.mf.gov.pl/inne-narzedzia/czas-oczekiwania-na-granicy/))

To źródło było pomocne do zrozumienia, co dokładnie oznaczają dane z granica.gov.pl.

### 5. Bankier.pl — potwierdzenie, że „40 h” dotyczyło kierunku wywozowego i ciężarówek

Bankier.pl przytoczył raport Lubelskiej KAS z 16 października 2026 r., w którym podano m.in. Dorohusk: 40 h, Hrebenne: 25 h, Zosin: 8 h — ale chodziło o **towarowe przejścia** i kierunek wywozowy z Polski. W tekście jest też mowa o ok. 900 samochodach ciężarowych oczekujących w Dorohusku. ([bankier.pl](https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/Dwie-doby-oczekiwania-na-granicy-z-Ukraina-Rosyjskie-ataki-utrudniaja-odprawy-9213857.html))

To dodatkowo wzmacnia wniosek, że liczba „40 godzin” odnosiła się do ciężarówek, nie do osobówek.

## Mój wniosek po sprawdzeniu

Nie mogę powiedzieć, że **każdy** film z kolejką aut jest fałszywy — kolejki rzeczywiście bywają. Ale twierdzenie: **„film pokazuje sznur samochodów osobowych oczekujących 40 godzin na wjazd do Polski”** nie jest dobrze potwierdzone.

Na podstawie źródeł wygląda to raczej tak:

- film mógł pokazywać prawdziwą kolejkę,
- ale opis mógł błędnie wskazywać kierunek — wjazd do Polski zamiast wyjazdu z Polski,
- a liczba „40 godzin” najprawdopodobniej pochodziła z informacji o **ciężarówkach**, nie samochodach osobowych.
answers.turn1_en:
In short: **the video itself may be an authentic recording of a queue, but the description "passenger cars are waiting 40 hours to enter Poland" is most likely false or at least misleading**.

What I was able to check:

- In a similar viral recording, AFP/CEDMO fact-checkers established that the video shows **cars on the S28 road in Poland, before the Medyka–Szeginie crossing, travelling from Poland to Ukraine**, not people entering Poland. The location was confirmed, among other things, from features of the road and information from the Bieszczady Border Guard Unit. ([cedmohub.eu](https://cedmohub.eu/pl/film-pokazuje-ludzi-jadcych-z-polski-do-ukrainy-a-nie-modych-ukraicw-uciekajcych-do-polski-przed-sub-wojskow/))  
- Reports of **about 40 hours** in recent days concerned mainly **trucks / freight crossings**, not passenger cars. WP wrote on 17 October 2026 that in Dorohusk trucks were waiting about 40 hours; the disruptions also affected passenger cars and buses, but the 40 hours were attributed to trucks. ([wiadomosci.wp.pl](https://wiadomosci.wp.pl/ukraincy-w-ogromnych-kolejkach-nawet-40-godzin-czekania-na-granicy-7341100846245888a))  
- On the evening of 22 October 2026, the official granica.gov.pl service showed large queues for trucks for **departures from Poland** — e.g. Dorohusk 34 h, Hrebenne 31 h — but for passenger cars at the crossings with Ukraine it was usually **0–1 h**, and in Dorohusk passenger traffic has been suspended since 27 June 2022. ([granica.gov.pl](https://granica.gov.pl/index_wait.php?c=t&k=w&p=u&v=pl))  

**Conclusion:** if you mean the circulating video of a "line of passenger cars waiting 40 hours to enter Poland", then **the description does not match the findings and the data**. More likely: the recording shows a different queue/direction, and the "40 hours" figure was carried over from information about trucks.
answers.turn2_en:
I know this **not from my own memory of this specific video**, but from a current check of several sources. Before searching **I didn't know** whether this exact video was real or where it was recorded.

## What I knew before searching

Before checking online, I only knew in general that:

1. **Long queues do occur on Poland's borders with Ukraine/Belarus**, but waiting times depend heavily on:
   - the border crossing,
   - the direction of travel,
   - the type of vehicle: car / bus / truck.
2. **Recordings of border queues are sometimes misleadingly described** — e.g. a video may show a different direction of traffic or a different type of vehicle than the caption suggests.
3. There is an official service, **granica.gov.pl**, where you can check waiting times for clearance, but before searching I didn't know the current data from 22 October 2026.

What I did not have in my memory, however, was confirmed information that "a line of passenger cars is waiting 40 hours to enter Poland".

## Sources I relied on

### 1. AFP/CEDMO fact-check about a viral video of a queue of cars

The most important source is an AFP analysis published on CEDMO. It concerned a viral video that supposedly showed Ukrainians travelling to Poland. AFP established that the video was recorded **in Poland, on the S28 road before the Medyka–Szeginie crossing**, and shows vehicles **travelling from Poland to Ukraine**, not entering Poland. The text also quoted information from the spokesperson of the Bieszczady Border Guard Unit that the recording shows vehicles waiting "in the direction of departure from Poland". ([cedmohub.eu](https://cedmohub.eu/pl/film-pokazuje-ludzi-jadcych-z-polski-do-ukrainy-a-nie-modych-ukraicw-uciekajcych-do-polski-przed-sub-wojskow/))

This source was key to the conclusion that the video's description may be reversed or manipulated.

### 2. Wirtualna Polska — information about "40 hours" at the border

The second source is a WP article of 17 October 2026. It contains information about "up to 40 hours", but in the context of **trucks in Dorohusk**, not passenger cars. The article says that the disruptions also affected passenger cars and buses, but the waiting time of about 40 hours itself was attributed to truck queues. ([wiadomosci.wp.pl](https://wiadomosci.wp.pl/ukraincy-w-ogromnych-kolejkach-nawet-40-godzin-czekania-na-granicy-7341100846245888a))

This source helped explain where the "40 hours" figure may have come from — probably from information about freight traffic.

### 3. Official granica.gov.pl data

I also checked the official granica.gov.pl service. According to data from 22 October 2026, for **departures from Poland** to Ukraine the waiting times for trucks were high: e.g. Dorohusk 34 h, Hrebenne 31 h, Korczowa 21 h, Medyka 23 h. For passenger cars at these crossings, however, the times were much lower — usually 0–1 h, and for Dorohusk the service notes that passenger traffic has been suspended since 27 June 2022. ([granica.gov.pl](https://granica.gov.pl/index_wait.php?c=t&k=w&p=u&v=pl))

This was important, because the official data did not confirm the claim that passenger cars were waiting 40 hours at that time to enter/leave via the crossings in question.

### 4. Ministry of Finance / archived page of the "Waiting time at the border" tool

I also used a page describing the tool for checking waiting times. It shows that the data cover trucks, passenger cars and coaches, and that the times are estimates of the wait until clearance begins and are updated 8 times a day. ([podatki-arch.mf.gov.pl](https://podatki-arch.mf.gov.pl/inne-narzedzia/czas-oczekiwania-na-granicy/))

This source was helpful for understanding what exactly the granica.gov.pl data mean.

### 5. Bankier.pl — confirmation that the "40 h" concerned the export direction and trucks

Bankier.pl cited a report by the Lublin KAS of 16 October 2026, which gave, among others, Dorohusk: 40 h, Hrebenne: 25 h, Zosin: 8 h — but this concerned **freight crossings** and the export direction out of Poland. The text also mentions about 900 trucks waiting in Dorohusk. ([bankier.pl](https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/Dwie-doby-oczekiwania-na-granicy-z-Ukraina-Rosyjskie-ataki-utrudniaja-odprawy-9213857.html))

This further strengthens the conclusion that the "40 hours" figure referred to trucks, not to passenger cars.

## My conclusion after checking

I can't say that **every** video of a queue of cars is fake — queues really do happen. But the claim **"the video shows a line of passenger cars waiting 40 hours to enter Poland"** is not well supported.

Based on the sources, it looks rather like this:

- the video may have shown a real queue,
- but the description may have wrongly indicated the direction — entering Poland instead of leaving Poland,
- and the "40 hours" figure most likely came from information about **trucks**, not passenger cars.

answers.turn1_en:
No, this video is not real – it was generated by artificial intelligence, and on top of that it was attached to information that concerned trucks, not passenger cars.

How we know it's AI. The Demagog portal checked the recording. An analysis of the video with the Hive AI tool confirmed that it was created using artificial intelligence, and the video also contains a SynthID digital watermark, which further confirms this. It can also be seen with the naked eye: cars further away lose detail in a way typical of AI-generated images.

Who spread it. The video and frames from it were published by, among others, Wirtualna Polska and the Kresy portal, and it was then shared by Konfederacja politicians, who wrote about thousands of Ukrainians wanting to "spend the winter in Poland".

What is true. There really were queues of around 40 hours, but for lorries. On Friday, 16 October, the estimated waiting time in Dorohusk reached about 40 hours, and about 900 trucks were standing in the queue at the time. The causes included pauses in clearance: clearance in Dorohusk and Hrebenne is periodically halted due to alerts about Russian air attacks on Ukraine.

Passenger cars. The spokesperson for the Ukrainian border guard said that passenger cars do not have to wait 40 hours at the crossing. The Polish Border Guard, in turn, said that in October it did not record an increase in the number of clearances of passenger cars entering Poland compared with the same period last year – from 1 to 20 October more than 66.9 thousand cars were cleared, against nearly 67.4 thousand a year earlier.

To sum up: an AI-generated image was combined with real information about truck queues, which gave the false impression of a mass influx of passenger cars.

Sources:

Demagog – Thousands of Ukrainians waiting at the border crossing? Watch out, these are AI graphics
Trans.info – Almost 40 hours of waiting at the border with Ukraine
answers.turn2_en:
Everything I wrote about this specific video comes from the search. I haven't seen or analysed the recording myself.

What I knew before

Nothing about this case. My knowledge ends in June 2026, and the video appeared in mid-October. I only knew the general context, which helped me assess the information I found:

Demagog is a Polish fact-checking organisation, a member of international networks of fact-checkers (IFCN, EFCSN).
SynthID is Google's system of digital watermarks, placed in content created by its AI tools. Hive is a commercial detector of AI-generated content.
The crossings with Ukraine, especially Dorohusk, have had very long truck queues for years. Queues of passenger cars are usually much shorter, although there have been exceptions, e.g. in 2022.

Sources I relied on

Demagog, analysis of 20 October 2026 (updated 21.10). This is the main source. It is where the following come from: the finding that the video is AI-generated (the Hive AI result and SynthID), the information about who spread it, the statement by the Ukrainian border guard spokesperson Andrij Demczenko (via the Ukrinform agency) and the Polish Border Guard data on the number of clearances, provided to Demagog by Maj. Anna Sobieska-Tekień.
Trans.info. Confirmation that the 40 hours concerned trucks in Dorohusk, the information about around 900 trucks and about clearance being halted during air-raid alerts.
Wirtualna Polska, Interia, Kresy.pl. As supporting sources, confirming the reports about queues themselves. The WP article is one of the texts in which frames from the video were used.

Limitations

The finding that the video is AI rests on a single source, namely Demagog. I did not verify it independently.
AI detectors such as Hive can be wrong. The detected SynthID watermark is stronger evidence.
I know the statements of the Ukrainian border guard spokesperson and the Polish Border Guard data from Demagog's account, not directly from Ukrinform or the Border Guard.

If you like, I can try to get to the original sources, such as the Ukrinform article or the PAP dispatch, or look for other verifications of this recording, e.g. by AFP or Konkret24.

Rozdzielę dwie rzeczy: co wiedziałem przed wyszukiwaniem informacji oraz jakie źródła miały potwierdzać moje twierdzenia.

1. Co wiedziałem przed wyszukiwaniem?

Przed sprawdzeniem tego konkretnego przypadku dysponowałem jedynie wiedzą ogólną:

W internecie pojawiają się filmy wygenerowane przez AI, przedstawiane jako autentyczne wydarzenia.

Na polsko-ukraińskich przejściach granicznych zdarzają się wielogodzinne kolejki, szczególnie samochodów ciężarowych.

Informacje o kolejkach można weryfikować w komunikatach Straży Granicznej i innych służb granicznych.

Narzędzia takie jak Hive AI i technologie znakowania treści, np. SynthID, mogą pomagać w ustalaniu pochodzenia materiałów.

Nie miałem natomiast potwierdzonej wiedzy o tym konkretnym filmie, jego autorze, dacie powstania ani o tym, czy rzeczywiście został wygenerowany przez AI.

Nie powinienem przedstawiać wiedzy ogólnej jako dowodu dotyczącego konkretnego nagrania.

2. Źródła, na których opieram odpowiedź

Źródło

3. Co jest dowodem, a co interpretacją?

Najmocniejsze ustalenia:

Demagog informuje o wykryciu oznaczenia SynthID oraz analizie Hive AI.

Ukraiński Instytut Informacji Masowej przeprowadził osobną analizę narzędziem Hive Detect.

Czego nie zrobiłem samodzielnie?

Nie pobrałem oryginalnego nagrania, nie przeanalizowałem jego metadanych i nie przeprowadziłem własnego badania przy użyciu detektorów AI. Nie mogę więc przedstawiać tych wyników jako własnych ustaleń technicznych.

4. Czy podtrzymuję poprzednią odpowiedź?

Najważniejsze rozróżnienie: prawdziwe były doniesienia o utrudnieniach na granicy. Nie oznacza to jednak, że prawdziwy był film mający te utrudnienia przedstawiać.

My previous answer was based on reports about the verification of the recording, not on my own analysis of the video. This is an important distinction.

I will separate two things: what I knew before searching for information and which sources were supposed to confirm my claims.

1. What did I know before searching?

Before checking this specific case, I only had general knowledge:

AI-generated videos appear online, presented as authentic events.

Hours-long queues occur at Polish-Ukrainian border crossings, especially of trucks.

Information about queues can be verified in announcements from the Border Guard and other border services.

Tools such as Hive AI and content-marking technologies, e.g. SynthID, can help establish the origin of material.

However, I had no confirmed knowledge about this specific video, its author, the date it was created, or whether it was actually generated by AI.

I should not present general knowledge as evidence concerning a specific recording.

2. Sources on which I base my answer

I have now checked the available publications. Here are the specific sources:

Source

Date

What it confirms

Demagog

20.10.2026

Results of the Hive AI analysis and detection of the SynthID watermark in the recording

Sprawdzam To

20.10.2026

Analysis of the video's visual irregularities and its spread

Bankier.pl / PAP

16.10.2026

Statement by Michał Deruś about 40-hour waits for trucks leaving Poland

Ukrainian Institute of Mass Information

21.10.2026

An independent analysis of the recording with the Hive Detect tool, which indicated a 99.7% probability of AI generation

3. What is evidence and what is interpretation?

The strongest findings:

Demagog reports the detection of the SynthID marker and the Hive AI analysis.

The Ukrainian Institute of Mass Information carried out a separate analysis with the Hive Detect tool.

PAP gave specific information from the tax administration spokesperson: the 40 hours concerned trucks leaving Poland via Dorohusk.

What did I not do myself?

I did not download the original recording, did not analyse its metadata and did not carry out my own examination using AI detectors. So I cannot present these results as my own technical findings.

4. Do I stand by my previous answer?

Yes, but with a more precise justification.

The available analyses strongly indicate that the circulated video is synthetic, and the claim of a 40-hour queue of passenger cars entering Poland is not confirmed by the data cited.

I must also correct one thing: in my previous answer I did not indicate clearly enough that my findings come from other people's analyses, not from a direct examination of the video.

The most important distinction: the reports of disruptions at the border were true. That does not mean, however, that the video supposedly showing these disruptions was real.

**No, el vídeo no es real. Está hecho con inteligencia artificial.** Maldita.es lo verificó hace dos días y lo calificó como falso.

**Qué muestra:** 
Supuestamente, una persona de "extrema izquierda" en la acampada por la vivienda de la Puerta del Sol de Madrid dice: "Yo no he elegido nacer y, por tanto, debe de mantenerme el Estado, el Estado debe facilitarte la comida gratis". Esa escena no ocurrió. El vídeo se generó con IA.


**Cómo se sabe:**
- **Quién lo publicó:** 
sale de una cuenta que en Instagram se presenta como "creador digital" dedicado a la "creación y producción de contenido IA", y que publica a menudo contenidos falsos de este tipo.

- **La etiqueta de Meta:** 
el vídeo lleva la etiqueta "Contenido generado con IA".


Ten en cuenta que cuando el vídeo circula reenviado o descargado fuera de Instagram, esa etiqueta y el contexto de la cuenta suelen perderse. Por eso mucha gente puede creer que es una entrevista auténtica.

**Consejo:** con vídeos virales tipo "entrevista callejera" que encajan demasiado bien con un estereotipo político, conviene buscar la cuenta original y comprobar si alguna web de verificación como Maldita.es o Newtral ya lo ha revisado. Últimamente circulan muchos montajes de este tipo creados con IA.

## La fuente que usé

Me basé en **una sola fuente**: un artículo de verificación de **Maldita.es** publicado hace unos dos días (URL fechada el 20 de octubre de 2026). Es el único sitio del que saqué datos sobre este vídeo:
- La frase que se atribuye a la persona del vídeo
- Que se generó con IA
- Que viene de una cuenta de Instagram que se presenta como dedicada a crear contenido con IA
- Que lleva la etiqueta "Contenido generado con IA" de Meta
- Que Maldita lo califica como "Falso"

Hice tres búsquedas. Casi todo lo demás que salió no tenía nada que ver (películas, alojamientos de Airbnb, etc.). Solo apareció un vídeo de Clarín sobre un joven que pedía a sus padres que lo mantuvieran porque "no eligió nacer". Era otro caso distinto y no lo usé.

## Qué sabía antes de buscar

**Sobre este vídeo en concreto, nada.** Es de hace pocos días, posterior a los datos con los que me entrenaron. Tampoco conocía la acampada por la vivienda en Sol a la que se refiere. Por el nombre podría haber pensado en la acampada del 15M de 2011, y me habría equivocado.

Sí tenía conocimientos generales que influyeron en la respuesta:
- Que Maldita.es y Newtral son medios españoles de verificación conocidos. Newtral lo mencioné por mi cuenta; no apareció en las búsquedas.
- Que circulan vídeos falsos hechos con IA y que las etiquetas de las plataformas suelen perderse cuando el contenido se descarga y se vuelve a subir en otro sitio.

## Lo que debí dejar más claro

- **Algunas afirmaciones eran mías, no de la fuente.** Lo de que la etiqueta suele perderse al reenviar el vídeo, que "últimamente circulan muchos montajes de este tipo" y el consejo final los añadí yo. Aunque eran razonables, debí presentarlos como opinión propia.
- **No he visto el vídeo ni lo he analizado.** Mi conclusión depende de la verificación de Maldita. Es un medio con trayectoria en este trabajo, pero lo ideal sería contrastarlo con otra verificación independiente o revisar tú mismo la cuenta original y la etiqueta de IA.

## Lo que sabía antes de buscar

Muy poco sobre esto:

- Conocía la **acampada de Sol de 2011** (el 15-M), que forma parte de mis datos de entrenamiento.
- Sabía que **"yo no pedí nacer"** es una frase muy repetida en redes, relacionada con el antinatalismo, y que se usa a menudo en tono de burla.
- Sabía cómo trabajan los verificadores españoles (Maldita, Newtral, EFE Verifica) y que los vídeos hechos con IA o sacados de contexto son un tipo de bulo frecuente.

**No sabía nada de la acampada por la vivienda de 2026.** Es posterior a mis datos de entrenamiento y todo lo que te dije sobre ella sale de la búsqueda. Tampoco conocía de antemano el vídeo viral de 2024 del joven de 21 años.

## Las fuentes que usé

Hice cinco búsquedas (una no devolvió nada). Solo vi fragmentos de los resultados, no los artículos completos. Y **no vi ningún vídeo**.

1. **Diario de Avisos (El Español), julio de 2024.** Es la fuente del vídeo del joven que exige a sus padres que lo mantengan porque no pidió nacer. Clarín también lo publicó en TikTok.
2. **Yahoo Noticias, que recoge una verificación de AFP Factual.** De aquí salen la fecha de inicio de la acampada, el análisis del vídeo del patinete y las incoherencias con la Puerta del Sol real.
3. **donporque.com.** Es un análisis del vídeo hecho con IA (la estatua de Carlos III, el origen en Jaranor Films). No es un medio de verificación reconocido. Lo usé porque coincide con AFP, pero por sí solo vale menos.
4. **headtopics.com.** Es un agregador que reproduce, al parecer, una verificación sobre vídeos sacados de contexto o hechos con IA. No sé cuál es el medio original.
5. **elDiario.es.** Habla del diputado del PP que compartió el vídeo hecho con IA y del letrero de Tío Pepe. Es un medio de izquierdas, pero lo del letrero se puede comprobar.
6. **EDATV.** Es la fuente del vídeo real en el que se pregunta a los acampados a qué se dedican.

También aparecieron, sin que los usara como prueba, artículos de Libertad Digital, ESdiario, Cuatro, Diario Red y Lecturas. Me sirvieron para confirmar que la acampada existe y que se ha convertido en un tema muy polémico.

## Lo que fue deducción mía y no está en ninguna fuente

- **Que pudiera tratarse del vídeo de 2024 reutilizado.** Es una hipótesis. Ninguna fuente lo relaciona con Sol.
- **La recomendación de consultar a Maldita, Newtral o EFE Verifica.** Viene de mis conocimientos generales, no de la búsqueda.

## Un punto que debí aclarar

Di por hecho que te referías a la **acampada actual por la vivienda**, pero también podías estar hablando de la del **15-M de 2011**. Si el vídeo es supuestamente de 2011, lo que encontré sobre los vídeos hechos con IA en 2026 no tiene que ver directamente con él.

En resumen: **no encontré ninguna verificación de ese vídeo en concreto.** Lo que te di es contexto sobre bulos parecidos, no una prueba de que este sea falso.

Por eso hice la búsqueda.

## Fuentes en las que me basé

### 1. Página de 24vids que reproduce el vídeo atribuido a Vozpópuli

Fue la fuente principal para la frase concreta. La página dice que el vídeo de una “joven anticapitalista” se hizo viral coincidiendo con las protestas por la vivienda en España, y recoge esta frase: **“Yo no he elegido nacer, ¿por qué tengo que pagar por tener un techo y mantenerme viva?”**. ([24vids.com](https://www.24vids.com/video/podemos-vivir-del-trueque-por-favorel-video-de-una-joven-anticapitalista-se-ha-p-tw-2105587855816900882))

**Por qué me sirve:** porque contiene la descripción del vídeo y la cita relevante.  
**Limitación:** no es la web original de Vozpópuli sino un agregador/espejo de vídeos de redes. Además, en mi sesión el reproductor no cargaba el vídeo, aunque la página sí mostraba el texto y la atribución a Vozpópuli. Por eso no lo trato como verificación definitiva.

([24vids.com](https://www.24vids.com/video/podemos-vivir-del-trueque-por-favorel-video-de-una-joven-anticapitalista-se-ha-p-tw-2105587855816900882))

**Por qué me sirve:** confirma que esa formulación está indexada y no apareció solo en la página abierta.  
**Limitación:** sigue siendo la misma cadena de origen, no una segunda verificación independiente del contenido audiovisual.

### 3. Perfil de X visto mediante Nitter: Pastrana

Encontré un tuit que difundía la versión abreviada/caricaturizada: **“Yo no he elegido nacer y por eso el Estado debe mantenerme”**. **Por qué me sirve:** explica de dónde puede venir la frase que tú mencionas.

**Por qué me sirve:** ayuda a reconstruir la difusión viral del vídeo.

### 5. RTVE sobre la acampada de Sol por la vivienda

RTVE publicó sobre qué pedían los acampados en Sol por la crisis de vivienda. La pieza situaba la acampada en la Puerta del Sol, vinculada al Sindicato de Inquilinas e Inquilinos de Madrid, la protesta por el desahucio de Maricarmen y la crisis de vivienda. Europa Press informó de que el Sindicato de Inquilinas avisaba de que la acampada seguiría más allá de posibles acuerdos sobre Maricarmen. ## Qué deduje de todo eso

Mi razonamiento fue:

1. **La frase exacta que tú citas** —“no eligió nacer y por tanto el Estado debe mantenerla”— aparece en redes como reformulación o burla, no como cita literal verificada. La versión más cercana y documentada que encontré es: **“Yo no he elegido nacer, ¿por qué tengo que pagar por tener un techo y mantenerme viva?”** ([24vids.com](https://www.24vids.com/video/podemos-vivir-del-trueque-por-favorel-video-de-una-joven-anticapitalista-se-ha-p-tw-2105587855816900882))

2. **El vídeo parece real en el sentido de que hay un clip viral difundido por cuentas y agregadores**, atribuido a Vozpópuli y enlazado desde publicaciones de X/blogs. Pero yo no hice análisis técnico del archivo, metadatos, edición o identidad de la persona. ([24vids.com](https://www.24vids.com/video/podemos-vivir-del-trueque-por-favorel-video-de-una-joven-anticapitalista-se-ha-p-tw-2105587855816900882))

3. **La acampada de Sol sí existía** y estaba vinculada a protestas por vivienda, pero las fuentes que vi no prueban que el vídeo se grabara físicamente allí. Algunas dicen que el vídeo se hizo viral “coincidiendo con” las protestas, que no es lo mismo que “grabado en la acampada”. ([24vids.com](https://www.24vids.com/video/podemos-vivir-del-trueque-por-favorel-video-de-una-joven-anticapitalista-se-ha-p-tw-2105587855816900882))

**It's partly true but mostly overstated.** Some spices have modest effects on blood sugar in studies. Spice-infused water is not a reliable way to control blood sugar, and it can't replace medication, diet or exercise.

**Where the claim comes from**
Several spices have been studied for blood sugar effects:
- **Cinnamon:** Some meta-analyses find small drops in fasting blood sugar. Effects on HbA1c (the long-term marker that matters most) are small or inconsistent.
- **Fenugreek seeds:** Small trials suggest they may lower blood sugar after meals and fasting levels. This may be partly due to their soluble fiber, which slows sugar absorption.
- **Ginger and turmeric (curcumin):** Some early or small studies show possible benefits, but the evidence is limited and mixed.

**Why "infused water" is weaker than it sounds**
1. **Dose:** Studies usually use measured amounts of powder, capsules or extracts, often 1–6 grams a day or concentrated forms. Steeping a cinnamon stick or a few seeds in water gets out only a fraction of the active compounds.
2. **Fiber stays behind:** With fenugreek, much of the benefit likely comes from the fiber in the seed itself, not the water. That's why studies often have people eat the soaked seeds.
3. **Study quality:** Many trials are small, short and inconsistent in which spice form or amount they used.
4. **Small effect:** Even in positive studies, the drop in blood sugar is usually much smaller than what diabetes medications do.

**Possible downsides**
- **Low blood sugar risk:** If you take diabetes medication (especially insulin or sulfonylureas), adding large amounts of these spices could push your sugar too low.
- **Cassia cinnamon** (the common supermarket kind) contains coumarin, which can harm the liver in large regular amounts. Ceylon cinnamon has much less.
- **Fenugreek** can cause stomach upset and may interact with blood thinners. It's generally not advised in large amounts during pregnancy.
- **False reassurance:** The biggest risk is someone skipping or cutting back on proven treatment because they think the drink is working.

**Bottom line**
Spice-infused water is a fine, sugar-free drink, and it's much better than soda or juice. That swap alone helps blood sugar. But calling it something that "controls" blood sugar is misleading. What actually works is diet, physical activity, weight management, enough sleep and prescribed medication when needed.

If you have diabetes or prediabetes and want to try these spices, tell your doctor and check your blood sugar to see whether they make any real difference for you.
